sentences.zh: 盧洪春，字思仁，東陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Hongchun, style Siren, was a native of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hongchun, styled Siren, came from Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 父仲佃，廣西布政使。

translations.literal: His father Zhongtian was Provincial Administrative Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongtian had served as provincial administrative commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 洪春舉萬歷五年進士，授旌德知縣，擢禮部祠祭主事。

translations.literal: Hongchun passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli, was appointed magistrate of Jingde, and was promoted to Principal Officer of Sacrificial Worship in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hongchun passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Wanli reign, was appointed magistrate of Jingde, and rose to principal officer of sacrificial worship in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十四年十月，帝久不視朝，洪春上疏曰：「陛下自九月望後，連日免朝，前日又詔頭眩體虛，暫罷朝講。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourteenth year, the emperor had long ceased to hold court. Hongchun submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty, since the full moon of the ninth month, has day after day excused court; the other day an edict also announced dizziness and bodily weakness and a temporary suspension of court lectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourteenth year, the emperor had long ceased to hold court. Hongchun submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty, since the full moon of the ninth month, has excused court day after day; only recently an edict announced dizziness and bodily weakness and a temporary suspension of court lectures.

sentences.zh: 時享太廟，遣官恭代，且云『非敢偷逸，恐弗成禮』。

translations.literal: When it came time to offer sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, you sent officials to perform the rites in your stead, and even said, 'It is not that we dare be idle—we fear the rites may not be properly accomplished.'
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple fell due, you sent officials to perform the rites in your stead, adding that you "dare not be idle" but fear the ceremony might not be properly completed.

sentences.zh: 臣愚捧讀，驚惶欲涕。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject, on reverently reading this, was struck with alarm and nearly brought to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject read this with alarm and was nearly brought to tears.

sentences.zh: 夫禮莫重於祭，而疾莫甚於虛。

translations.literal: Of all rites none is weightier than sacrifice, and of all ailments none is graver than debility.
translations.idiomatic: Of all rites none is weightier than sacrifice, and of all ailments none is graver than debility.

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋鼎盛，諸癥皆非所宜有。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is in the prime of life; such symptoms are none of them what you ought to suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is in the prime of life; such symptoms are not what you ought to suffer at all.

sentences.zh: 不宜有而有之，上傷聖母之心，下駭臣民之聽，而又因以廢祖宗大典，臣不知陛下何以自安也。

translations.literal: That you should suffer them when you ought not wounds the heart of the empress dowager, alarms the ears of officials and people alike, and moreover leads to the abandonment of the great ancestral ceremonies—I do not know how Your Majesty can rest easy.
translations.idiomatic: That you should suffer them when you ought not wounds the empress dowager's heart, alarms officials and commoners alike, and leads to the abandonment of the great ancestral ceremonies—I do not see how Your Majesty can be at ease.

sentences.zh: 抑臣所聞，更有異者。

translations.literal: Yet what I have heard is still more strange.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I have heard is stranger still.

sentences.zh: 先二十六日傳旨免朝，即聞人言籍籍，謂陛下試馬傷額，故引疾自諱。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth, when the order went out excusing court, rumor at once ran thick that Your Majesty had been injured in the forehead while testing horses, and therefore invoked illness to conceal it.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth, when the order excusing court went out, rumor at once ran thick that Your Majesty had injured your forehead while testing horses and therefore invoked illness to conceal it.

sentences.zh: 果如人言，則以一時馳騁之樂，而昧周身之防，其為患猶淺。

translations.literal: If the rumor is true, then for a moment's pleasure in galloping you neglected the preservation of your person—the harm would still be comparatively slight.
translations.idiomatic: If the rumor is true, then for a moment's pleasure in galloping you neglected to guard your person—the harm would still be comparatively slight.

sentences.zh: 倘如聖諭，則以目前衽席之娛，而忘保身之術，其為患更深。

translations.literal: If it is as the sacred edict says, then for present comfort on couch and mat you have forgotten the art of self-preservation—the harm runs deeper still.
translations.idiomatic: If it is as the sacred edict says, then for present comfort on couch and mat you have forgotten the art of preserving yourself—the harm runs deeper still.

sentences.zh: 若乃為聖德之累，則均焉而已。

translations.literal: As for being a burden upon Your Majesty's sagely virtue, the one amounts to the same as the other.
translations.idiomatic: As for being a burden on Your Majesty's sagely virtue, the one is as bad as the other.

sentences.zh: 且陛下毋謂身居九重，外廷莫知。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty must not suppose that dwelling deep within the palace, the outer court knows nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty must not suppose that, dwelling deep within the palace, the outer court knows nothing.

sentences.zh: 天子起居，豈有寂然無聞於人者？

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's comings and goings—can they be utterly unheard by anyone?
translations.idiomatic: Can the Son of Heaven's comings and goings pass entirely without anyone hearing of them?

sentences.zh: 然莫敢直言以導陛下，則將順之意多，而愛敬之心薄也。

translations.literal: Yet if none dares speak plainly to guide Your Majesty, then compliance is plentiful while reverent love runs thin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if none dares speak plainly to guide Your Majesty, compliance is plentiful while reverent love runs thin.

sentences.zh: 陛下平日遇頌諛必多喜，遇諫諍必多怒，一涉宮闈，嚴譴立至，孰肯觸諱，以蹈不測之禍哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty daily takes much pleasure in flattery and much offense at remonstrance; let the inner palace be touched and severe punishment follows at once—who would risk taboo and court unforeseen disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty daily takes much pleasure in flattery and much offense at remonstrance; touch the inner palace and severe punishment follows at once—who would risk taboo and court unforeseen disaster?

sentences.zh: 群臣如是，非主上福也。

translations.literal: When ministers are thus, it is no blessing to their sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers act thus, it is no blessing to their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以宗社為重，毋務矯托以滋疑。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty take the altars of state and grain as paramount and not insist on strained excuses that breed doubt.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty hold the altars of state and grain paramount and not insist on strained excuses that breed doubt.

sentences.zh: 力制此心，慎加防檢。

translations.literal: Strengthen restraint upon this heart and guard yourself with care.
translations.idiomatic: Restrain this heart and guard yourself with care.

sentences.zh: 勿以深宮燕閑有所恣縱，勿以左右近習有所假借，飭躬踐行，明示天下，以章律度，則天下萬世，將慕義無窮。

translations.literal: Do not indulge yourself in idle ease deep within the palace; do not lend yourself to those attendants close at hand. Order your person and act accordingly, make it manifest to all under heaven, and clarify law and measure—then for ten thousand generations the realm will admire righteousness without end.
translations.idiomatic: Do not indulge yourself in idle ease deep within the palace; do not lend yourself to attendants close at hand. Order your person and act accordingly, make your conduct manifest to all under heaven, and clarify law and measure—then for ten thousand generations the realm will admire righteousness without end.

sentences.zh: 較夫挾數用術，文過飾非，幾以聾瞽天下之耳目者，相去何如哉！」

translations.literal: How does this compare with grasping stratagem and wielding artifice, glossing faults and decking out errors, nearly deafening and blinding the ears and eyes of all under heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: How does this compare with grasping stratagem and wielding artifice, glossing over faults and decking out errors, nearly deafening and blinding the ears and eyes of all under heaven!"

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝震怒。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was shaken with rage.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was shaken with rage.

sentences.zh: 傳諭內閣百余言，極明謹疾遣官之故。

translations.literal: He transmitted more than a hundred characters of instruction to the Grand Secretariat, elaborating at length the reasons for excusing court on account of illness and dispatching officials.
translations.idiomatic: He transmitted more than a hundred characters of instruction to the Grand Secretariat, elaborating at length why he had excused court on account of illness and dispatched officials in his stead.

sentences.zh: 以洪春悖妄，命擬旨治罪。

translations.literal: Because Hongchun had been insolent and presumptuous, he ordered a draft rescript for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hongchun had been insolent and presumptuous, he ordered a draft rescript for his punishment.

sentences.zh: 閣臣擬奪官，仍論救。

translations.literal: The grand secretaries proposed deprivation of office while still interceding on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries proposed stripping him of office while still interceding on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，廷杖六十，斥為民。

translations.literal: The emperor would not agree; Hongchun received sixty strokes at court and was expelled as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree; Hongchun received sixty strokes at court and was expelled as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 諸給事中申救，忤旨，切讓。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries all pleaded for him; defying the edict, they were sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries all pleaded for him; defying the edict, they were sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 諸御史疏繼之，帝怒，奪俸有差。

translations.literal: The censors followed with successive memorials; the emperor grew angry and reduced salaries by varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The censors followed with successive memorials; the emperor grew angry and reduced their salaries by varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 洪春遂廢於家，久之卒。

translations.literal: Hongchun was thereby cast aside at home; after a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: Hongchun was thereby cast aside at home; after a long while he died.

sentences.zh: 光宗嗣位，贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded, Hongchun was posthumously given the title of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded to the throne, Hongchun was posthumously given the title of vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 御史範俊嘗陳時政。

translations.literal: Censor Fan Jun once submitted a memorial on current administration.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fan Jun once submitted a memorial on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝方疾，見俊疏中「防人欲」語，斥之。

translations.literal: The emperor was then ill; seeing in Jun's memorial the phrase "guard against human desire," he rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then ill; seeing in Jun's memorial the phrase "guard against human desire," he rejected it.

sentences.zh: 主事董基以諫內操謫官。

translations.literal: Principal Officer Dong Ji was demoted for remonstrating against inner-palace drill.
translations.idiomatic: Principal officer Dong Ji was demoted for remonstrating against inner-palace drill.

sentences.zh: 其後員外郎王就學因諫帝托疾不送梓宮，尋罷去。

translations.literal: Later, Vice Director Wang Jiuxue, for remonstrating that the emperor feigned illness and did not escort the spirit tablet, was soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, vice director Wang Jiuxue, for remonstrating that the emperor feigned illness and did not escort the spirit tablet, was soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 皆與洪春疏相類。

translations.literal: All were of the same sort as Hongchun's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: All were of the same sort as Hongchun's memorial.

sentences.zh: 範俊，字國士，高安人。

translations.literal: Fan Jun, style Guoshi, was a native of Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jun, styled Guoshi, came from Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 為義烏知縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: Serving as magistrate of Yiwu, he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Yiwu, he was summoned and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，陳時政十事，語皆切至，而中言「人欲宜防，力以靡曼麹蘗為戒」。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year he set forth ten points on current administration, all trenchant; among them he said that human desire should be guarded against and urged stern warning against dissipation and wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year he set forth ten points on current affairs, all trenchant; among them he urged that human desire be guarded against and warned sternly against dissipation and wine.

sentences.zh: 先是，慈寧宮災，給事中鄒元標疏陳六事，忤帝意。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cining Palace burned, Supervising Secretary Zou Yuanbiao memorialized six points and offended the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cining Palace burned, supervising secretary Zou Yuanbiao memorialized six points and offended the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及帝遘微疾，大臣方問安，而俊疏適入。

translations.literal: When the emperor contracted a slight illness and grand ministers were just paying their respects, Jun's memorial happened to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor contracted a slight illness and grand ministers were just paying their respects, Jun's memorial happened to arrive.

sentences.zh: 帝恚曰：「向未罪元標，致俊復爾，當重懲之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said in anger: "Because I did not punish Yuanbiao before, Jun has done the same again—he must be severely punished."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in anger: "Because I did not punish Yuanbiao before, Jun has done the same again—he must be severely punished."

sentences.zh: 申時行等擬鐫秩。

translations.literal: Shen Shixing and the others proposed reducing his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing and the others proposed reducing his rank.

sentences.zh: 帝猶怒，將各予杖。

translations.literal: The emperor was still angry and was about to have them all beaten.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still angry and was about to have them all beaten.

sentences.zh: 是夜大雷雨，明日朝門外水三尺余。

translations.literal: That night there was a great thunderstorm; the next day water outside the court gate stood more than three feet deep.
translations.idiomatic: That night there was a great thunderstorm; the next day water outside the court gate stood more than three feet deep.

sentences.zh: 帝怒少霽，時行等亦力救，乃斥為民。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger eased somewhat; Shen and the others also exerted themselves to save him, and Jun was expelled as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased somewhat; Shen and the others also exerted themselves to save him, and Jun was expelled as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 明年，給事中張維新請推用譴謫諸臣，詔許量移，惟俊不敘。

translations.literal: The following year Supervising Secretary Zhang Weixin asked that dismissed and demoted officials be promoted; an edict permitted them to be moved up in rank by degrees, but Jun alone was not restored.
translations.idiomatic: The following year supervising secretary Zhang Weixin asked that dismissed and demoted officials be promoted; an edict permitted them to be moved up in rank by degrees, but Jun alone was not restored.

sentences.zh: 給事中孫世禎、御史方萬山等言俊不宜獨遺，坐奪俸。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Sun Shizhen, Censor Fang Wanshan, and others said Jun ought not to be singled out for exclusion; they were penalized by reduction of salary.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Sun Shizhen, censor Fang Wanshan, and others said Jun ought not to be singled out for exclusion; they were penalized by reduction of salary.

sentences.zh: 自是屢薦不起，裏居數十年卒。

translations.literal: From then on, though recommended repeatedly, he was never recalled; he lived at home for decades and died.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, though recommended repeatedly, he was never recalled; he lived at home for decades and died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，復官，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign his office was restored; he was posthumously given Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign his office was restored; he was posthumously given vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 董基，字巢雄，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Dong Ji, style Chaoxiong, was a native of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ji, styled Chaoxiong, came from Ye County.

sentences.zh: 萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal officer in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal officer in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝集內豎三千人，授以戈甲，操於內廷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor assembled three thousand inner eunuchs, gave them halberds and armor, and drilled them within the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the emperor assembled three thousand inner eunuchs, gave them halberds and armor, and drilled them within the inner court.

sentences.zh: 尚書張學顏諫，不納。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Xueyan remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Xueyan remonstrated but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 基抗疏曰：「內廷清嚴地，無故聚三千之眾，輕以兇器嘗試，竊為陛下危之。

translations.literal: Ji submitted a forceful memorial saying: "The inner court is a place of strict purity; to gather three thousand men without cause and lightly try deadly weapons—I venture to say Your Majesty is endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Ji submitted a forceful memorial: "The inner court is a place of strict purity; to gather three thousand men without cause and lightly try deadly weapons—I must say Your Majesty is endangered.

sentences.zh: 陛下以為行幸山陵，有此三千人可無恐乎？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty think that when traveling to the imperial tombs, with these three thousand men you need fear nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty think that when traveling to the imperial tombs, with these three thousand men you need fear nothing?

sentences.zh: 不知此皆無當實用。

translations.literal: You do not know that they are wholly useless in practice.
translations.idiomatic: You do not know that they are wholly useless in practice.

sentences.zh: 設遇健卒勁騎，立見披靡，車駕不可恃以輕出也。

translations.literal: Suppose you met hardy troops and strong cavalry—they would at once be routed; the imperial carriage cannot be lightly ventured abroad relying on them.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose you met hardy troops and strong cavalry—they would at once be routed; the imperial carriage cannot be lightly ventured abroad relying on them.

sentences.zh: 夫此三千人安居美食，筋力柔靡，一旦使執銳衣堅，蒙寒犯暑，臣聞頃者竟日演練，中暍瀕死者數人，若輩未有不怨者。

translations.literal: These three thousand live at ease on fine food; their sinews are soft and lax. Suddenly to make them grasp sharp weapons and don hard armor, brave cold and suffer heat—I hear that in recent days, drilling all day long, several collapsed from heatstroke near death; such men cannot but resent it.
translations.idiomatic: These three thousand live at ease on fine food; their sinews are soft and lax. Suddenly to make them grasp sharp weapons and don hard armor, brave cold and suffer heat—I hear that in recent days, drilling all day long, several collapsed from heatstroke near death; such men cannot but resent it.

sentences.zh: 聚三千蓄怨之人於肘腋，危無逾此者。

translations.literal: To gather three thousand men nursing resentment at your elbow—danger cannot exceed this.
translations.idiomatic: To gather three thousand men nursing resentment at your elbow—danger cannot exceed this.

sentences.zh: 且自內操以來，賞賚已二萬金。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the inner drill began, rewards have already reached twenty thousand taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the inner drill began, rewards have already reached twenty thousand taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 長此不已，安有殫竭？

translations.literal: If this goes on without end, how can exhaustion be avoided?
translations.idiomatic: If this goes on without end, how can exhaustion be avoided?

sentences.zh: 有用之財，糜之無用之地，誠可惜也。」

translations.literal: Useful funds squandered upon a useless enterprise—truly it is pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: Useful funds squandered on a useless enterprise—truly it is pitiable."

sentences.zh: 疏入，忤旨，命貶二秩，調邊方。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it defied the edict; he was ordered demoted two ranks and transferred to the borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, it defied the edict; he was ordered demoted two ranks and transferred to the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 九卿、給事、御史交章論救，且請納基言，不聽。

translations.literal: The nine ministers, supervising secretaries, and censors submitted joint memorials in his defense and asked that Ji's words be adopted; they were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The nine ministers, supervising secretaries, and censors submitted joint memorials in his defense and asked that Ji's words be adopted; they were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 竟謫基萬全都司都事。

translations.literal: In the end Ji was demoted to Company Commander in the Wanquan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Ji was demoted to company commander in the Wanquan garrison.

sentences.zh: 明年，兵科給事中王致祥言：「祖宗法，非宿衛士不得持寸兵。

translations.literal: The next year Military Supervising Secretary Wang Zhixiang said: "By ancestral law none but palace guards may bear the smallest weapon.
translations.idiomatic: The next year military supervising secretary Wang Zhixiang said: "By ancestral law none but palace guards may bear the smallest weapon.

sentences.zh: 今授群不逞利器，出入禁門，禍不細。」

translations.literal: Now a disorderly throng is given sharp weapons and passes in and out of the forbidden gates—the misfortune is no small matter."
translations.idiomatic: Now a disorderly throng is given sharp weapons and passes in and out of the forbidden gates—the misfortune is no small matter."

sentences.zh: 大學士申時行亦語司禮監曰：「此事系禁廷，諸人擐甲執戈，未明而入。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing also spoke to the Directorate of Ceremonial: "This affair concerns the forbidden court. These men don armor and take up halberds, entering before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing also spoke to the Directorate of Ceremonial: "This affair concerns the forbidden court. These men don armor and take up halberds, entering before dawn.

sentences.zh: 設奸人竄其中，一旦緩急，外廷不得聞，宿衛不及備，此公等剝膚患也。」

translations.literal: If villains should slip among them, then in a sudden emergency the outer court would not hear, palace guards could not prepare in time—this is a calamity that flays your very skin."
translations.idiomatic: If villains should slip among them, then in a sudden emergency the outer court would not hear, palace guards could not prepare in time—this is a calamity that flays your very skin."

sentences.zh: 中官悚然，乘間力言。

translations.literal: The eunuchs were startled and seized an opening to speak forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs were startled and seized an opening to speak forcefully.

sentences.zh: 帝乃留致祥疏，即日罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor then kept Zhixiang's memorial and that same day abolished the drill.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then kept Zhixiang's memorial and that same day abolished the drill.

sentences.zh: 會謫降官皆量移，基亦遷南京禮部主事，終南京大理卿。

translations.literal: When demoted officials were all moved up in rank by degrees, Ji was also transferred to Principal Officer in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and ended as Nanjing Chief Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When demoted officials were all moved up in rank by degrees, Ji was also transferred to principal officer in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and ended as Nanjing chief minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 致祥，忻州人。

translations.literal: Zhixiang was a native of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang came from Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官右僉都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: He rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and served as Grand Coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice censor-in-chief and served as grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 王就學，字所敬，武進人。

translations.literal: Wang Jiuxue, style Suojing, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiuxue, styled Suojing, came from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fourteenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal officer in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal officer in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三王並封議起，朝論大嘩。

translations.literal: When debate arose over enfeoffing the three princes together, court opinion erupted.
translations.idiomatic: When debate arose over enfeoffing the three princes together, court opinion erupted.

sentences.zh: 就學，王錫爵門人也，偕同年生錢允元往規之，為流涕。

translations.literal: Jiuxue was a student of Wang Xijue; together with his year-mate Qian Yunyuan he went to admonish him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuxue was a student of Wang Xijue; together with his year-mate Qian Yunyuan he went to admonish him and wept.

sentences.zh: 會庶吉士李騰芳投錫爵書，與就學語相類。

translations.literal: At the same time Hanlin Bachelor Li Tengfang sent Xijue a letter with language akin to Jiuxue's.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Hanlin bachelor Li Tengfang sent Xijue a letter with language akin to Jiuxue's.

sentences.zh: 錫爵悟，並封詔得寢。

translations.literal: Xijue came to his senses, and the joint-enfeoffment edict was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue came to his senses, and the joint-enfeoffment edict was shelved.

sentences.zh: 就學改禮部，進員外郎，尋調吏部。

translations.literal: Jiuxue was transferred to the Ministry of Rites, advanced to vice director, and soon moved to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuxue was transferred to the Ministry of Rites, advanced to vice director, and soon moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，孝安陳太后梓宮發引，帝嫡母也，當送門外，以有疾，遣官代行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when the bier of Empress Dowager Xia'an Chen departed on its funeral procession—she was the emperor's legal mother—he ought to have seen her off beyond the gate; citing illness, he sent an official to go in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when the funeral procession of Empress Dowager Xia'an Chen departed, she being the emperor's legal mother, he should have escorted her beyond the gate; but pleading illness, he dispatched an official to perform the rite in his place.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎孫繼臯言之，帝怒，抵其疏於地。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Sun Jigao spoke of it; the emperor grew angry and dashed his memorial to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Sun Jigao remonstrated on the matter; the emperor flew into a rage and threw his memorial to the floor.

sentences.zh: 就學抗疏曰：「人子於親惟送死為大事。

translations.literal: Jiuxue submitted a forceful memorial saying: "For a son toward his parents, only seeing them off in death is the great affair.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuxue submitted a forceful memorial: [For a son, nothing toward his parents is greater than seeing them properly to their grave.

sentences.zh: 今乃靳一攀送，致聖孝不終。

translations.literal: Now you stint at one moment of clasping the bier to see them off, causing sacred filial piety to remain unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now Your Majesty withholds even a single moment at the coffin to bid farewell, leaving sacred filial piety incomplete.

sentences.zh: 豈獨有乖古禮，即聖心豈能自安。

translations.literal: How can this alone violate ancient rites—even the sacred heart, how can it be at ease with itself?
translations.idiomatic: This not only departs from ancient rites; how can Your Majesty's own heart find peace in it?

sentences.zh: 於此而不用其情，烏乎用其情？

translations.literal: If feeling is not applied here, whither is feeling to be applied?
translations.idiomatic: If filial feeling is not spent here, where then should it ever be spent?

sentences.zh: 於此而可忍，烏乎不可忍？

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what then cannot be borne?
translations.idiomatic: If this can be tolerated, what outrage could not be?

sentences.zh: 恐難以宣諸詔諭，書諸簡冊，傳示天下萬世也。」

translations.literal: I fear it will be hard to proclaim in edicts and proclamations, write in the bamboo slips and registers, and transmit to all under Heaven for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: I fear it will scarcely do to proclaim in edicts, inscribe in the annals, and show all under Heaven for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不省。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: ] The memorial was submitted, and the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 逾二年，詔甄別吏部諸郎，斥就學為民。

translations.literal: After more than two years, an edict ordered the sorting and ranking of the various bureau directors in the Ministry of Personnel, and Jiuxue was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: More than two years later, an edict ordered a review of the Ministry of Personnel's bureau directors, and Jiuxue was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died at home.

sentences.zh: 繼臯抗疏未幾，給事中劉道亨劾文選員外郎蔡夢麟紊銓政，並及繼臯。

translations.literal: Not long after Jigao's forceful memorial, Supervising Secretary Liu Daoheng impeached Selection Bureau Vice Director Cai Menglin for disordering appointment affairs, and also implicated Jigao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Jigao's forceful memorial, Supervising Secretary Liu Daoheng impeached Selection Bureau Vice Director Cai Menglin for corrupting appointment policy, implicating Jigao as well.

sentences.zh: 乞罷，不報。

translations.literal: He begged dismissal; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be removed from office, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 及三殿災，大臣自陳，皆慰留，獨繼臯致仕去。

translations.literal: When the three halls burned, the grand ministers each declared their own guilt; all were comforted and retained—only Jigao retired and left.
translations.idiomatic: When fire destroyed the three main halls, the grand ministers each submitted self-accusations; all were comforted and kept in office, but Jigao alone retired and departed.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 繼臯，字以德，無錫人。

translations.literal: Jigao, style Yide, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao, styled Yide, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年進士第一。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the second year of Wanli, ranking first.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place among jinshi graduates in the second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 李懋檜，字克蒼，安溪人。

translations.literal: Li Maohui, style Kechang, was a native of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maohui, styled Kechang, came from Anxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除六安知州，入為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Lu'an; he entered service as vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Lu'an, then entered the capital as vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，帝方憂旱，命所司條上便宜。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year the emperor was then worried about drought and ordered the relevant offices to list expedient measures item by item.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year, as the emperor was troubled by drought, he ordered the relevant offices to submit practical proposals.

sentences.zh: 懋檜及部郎劉復初等爭言皇貴妃及恭妃冊封事，章一日並上。

translations.literal: Maohui and section director Liu Fuchu and others competed to speak on the investiture of the Imperial Noble Consort and the Honored Consort; their memorials all went up on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Maohui, section director Liu Fuchu, and others all spoke out on the investiture of the Imperial Noble Consort and the Honored Consort, and their memorials were submitted together in a single day.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲加重譴，言者猶不已。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and wished to add heavier punishment, yet the memorialists still did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and wanted to punish them more severely, but the memorialists would not cease.

sentences.zh: 閣臣請帝詔諸曹建言止及所司職掌，且不得專達，以慰解帝意。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat members asked the emperor to proclaim that memorials from all offices should be limited to their departmental duties and must not reach the throne directly alone, so as to soothe and explain the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries asked the emperor to issue an edict limiting memorials to each office's proper jurisdiction and forbidding direct access to the throne, hoping to ease his anger.

sentences.zh: 居數日，帝亦霽威，諸疏皆留中。

translations.literal: After several days the emperor's wrath also cleared, and all the memorials were kept at court without action.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the emperor's anger subsided, and all the memorials were shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 而懋檜疏又有保聖躬、節內供、禦近習、開言路、議蠲振、慎刑罰、重舉刺、限田制七事，亦寢不行。

translations.literal: And Maohui's memorial also had seven items—safeguarding the sacred person, economizing inner supplies, guarding against close attendants, opening paths of speech, discussing tax remission and relief, being careful with punishments, emphasizing censorial investigation, and limiting landholding systems—all likewise were shelved without enactment.
translations.idiomatic: Maohui's memorial also proposed seven measures: protecting the emperor's health, reducing palace expenditures, guarding against close attendants, opening channels of remonstrance, discussing tax relief and famine aid, exercising restraint in punishment, strengthening censorial oversight, and imposing limits on landholding—all of which were likewise ignored.

sentences.zh: 明年，給事中邵庶因論誠意伯劉世延，刺及建言諸臣。

translations.literal: The next year, Supervising Secretary Shao Shu, in discussing Marquis of Chengyi Liu Shiyan, took a swipe that reached the memorialists.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Supervising Secretary Shao Shu, while discussing Marquis of Chengyi Liu Shiyan, took indirect aim at those who had submitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 懋檜上言：「庶因世延條奏，波及言者，欲概絕之。

translations.literal: Maohui submitted saying: "Shu, on the basis of Shiyan's memorial items, spread to the memorialists, wishing to cut them off entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Maohui submitted a memorial: [Drawing on Liu Shiyan's memorial, Shu has cast his net over those who speak out and would cut them off altogether.

sentences.zh: 『防人之口，甚於防川』，庶豈不聞斯語哉？

translations.literal: 'To stop men's mouths is more urgent than stopping a river'—surely Shu has heard this saying?
translations.idiomatic: 'To dam men's mouths is more perilous than damming a river'—can Shu truly never have heard this saying?

sentences.zh: 今天下民窮財殫，所在饑饉，山、陜、河南，婦子仳離，僵仆滿道，疾苦危急之狀，蓋有鄭俠所不能圖者，陛下不得聞且見也。

translations.literal: Today under Heaven the people are impoverished and finances exhausted; everywhere there is famine; in Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan, wives and children are torn apart and corpses lie full on the roads—the state of bitter suffering and urgent peril is such that even Zheng Xia could not depict it; Your Majesty cannot hear of it nor see it.
translations.idiomatic: Today the people are destitute and the treasury drained; famine is everywhere. In Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan, wives and children are torn apart and the dead litter the roads. The misery is beyond what even Zheng Xia's painting could capture, yet Your Majesty neither hears of it nor sees it.

sentences.zh: 邇者雷擊日壇，星墜如鬥，天變示儆於上；

translations.literal: Recently lightning struck the Altar of the Sun; a star fell like a dipper; heaven's changes show warning above;
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago lightning struck the Altar of the Sun and a star fell the size of a dipper—heaven's warnings are plain above;

sentences.zh: 畿輦之間，子弒父，仆殺主，人情乖離於下。

translations.literal: within the capital region, sons murdered fathers and servants killed masters—human relations are estranged below.
translations.idiomatic: within the capital, sons murder fathers and servants kill masters—human bonds are breaking apart below.

sentences.zh: 庶以為海內盡無可言已乎？

translations.literal: Does Shu think that within the seas all is already unspeakable?
translations.idiomatic: Does Shu imagine that throughout the realm there is truly nothing left worth saying?

sentences.zh: 夫在廷之臣，其為言官者十僅二三。

translations.literal: Of the ministers at court, those who are censorial officials are scarcely two or three in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Of the officials at court, only two or three in ten hold censorial posts.

sentences.zh: 言官不必皆智，不為言官者不必皆愚。

translations.literal: Censorial officials need not all be wise; those who are not censorial officials need not all be foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials are not all wise, and those who are not censorial officials are not all foolish.

sentences.zh: 無論往事，即如邇歲馮保、張居正交通亂政，其連章保留，頌功詡德，若陳三謨、曾士楚者，並出臺垣，而請劍引裾杖謫以去者，非庶僚則新進書生也。

translations.literal: Setting aside past affairs—even as in recent years Feng Bao and Zhang Juzheng colluded in disordering government: those who linked memorials begging retention and praised merits and extolled virtue, such as Chen Sanmo and Zeng Shichu, all came from the Censorate, while those who begged the sword, seized the robe, and were staff-beaten and banished to leave were none other than ordinary subordinates or newly entered literati.
translations.idiomatic: Leave aside earlier events: in recent years, when Feng Bao and Zhang Juzheng colluded to corrupt government, those who submitted linked memorials begging to keep them in power and praising their merits—men such as Chen Sanmo and Zeng Shichu—came from the Censorate, while those who begged the sword, seized the emperor's robe, and were beaten and banished were ordinary officials or newly appointed scholars.

sentences.zh: 果若庶言，天下幸無事則可，脫有不虞之變，陛下何從而知？

translations.literal: If it were truly as Shu says, if under Heaven fortunately nothing happened that would be fine; should there be unforeseen disaster, from where would Your Majesty learn of it?
translations.idiomatic: If Shu's view prevailed and all remained quiet, that would be well enough; but should unforeseen calamity arise, how would Your Majesty ever learn of it?

sentences.zh: 庶復以堂上官禁止司屬為得計，伏睹《大明律》，百工技藝之人，若有可言之事，直至御前奏聞，但有阻遏者斬。

translations.literal: Shu again took forbidding subordinates by their bureau superiors as a good scheme. I prostrate myself and view the Great Ming Code: men of all crafts and skills, if they have matters that may be spoken, may go straight before the throne to report; whoever obstructs them is beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Shu further treats it as sound policy for bureau chiefs to silence their subordinates. Yet I see in the Great Ming Code that artisans and craftsmen who have matters to report may go straight to the throne, and anyone who blocks them is to be executed.

sentences.zh: 《大明會典》及皇祖《臥碑》亦屢言之。

translations.literal: The Great Ming Institutes and the imperial ancestor's Sleeping Stele also speak of this repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Ming Institutes and the imperial ancestor's Sleeping Stele say the same again and again.

sentences.zh: 百工技藝之人，有言尚不敢阻，況諸司百執事乎？

translations.literal: For men of all crafts and skills, if they have words you still dare not obstruct—how much more the hundred officials of the various departments?
translations.idiomatic: If even artisans who speak up may not be obstructed, how much less may the officials of every department be silenced?

sentences.zh: 庶言一出，誌士解體，善言日壅，主上不得聞其過，群下無所獻其忠，禍天下必自庶始。

translations.literal: Once Shu's words come forth, men of resolve will lose cohesion; good words will daily be choked off; the sovereign will not hear his faults; the group below will have nowhere to offer loyalty—harm to all under Heaven must begin with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu's proposal is adopted, men of principle will lose heart, good counsel will be choked off day by day, the sovereign will hear nothing of his faults, and subordinates will have no way to offer loyal remonstrance. Disaster for the realm will begin with Shu.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲重百官越職之禁，不若嚴言官失職之罰。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must wish to reinforce the prohibition against officials overstepping their posts, better to be strict in punishment for censorial officials' dereliction of duty.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to tighten the ban on officials speaking outside their duties, it would be better to punish censorial officials who fail in their duty.

sentences.zh: 當言不言，坐以負君誤國之罪。

translations.literal: Where one should speak and does not speak, make guilty of the crime of betraying the sovereign and misleading the state.
translations.idiomatic: Those who ought to speak but remain silent should be charged with betraying the sovereign and misleading the state.

sentences.zh: 輕則記過，重則褫官。

translations.literal: In light cases, record the fault; in heavy cases, strip office.
translations.idiomatic: In minor cases they should be marked for fault; in serious cases they should be stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 科道當遷，一視其章奏多寡得失為殿最，則言官無不直言，庶官無事可言，出位之禁無庸，太平之效自致矣。」

translations.literal: When censorate officials face transfer, treat exclusively the abundance or scarcity and gain or loss of their memorials as ranking for assessment—then censorial officials will none fail to speak straight, ordinary officials will have no affairs to speak of, prohibitions against overstepping posts will be unnecessary, and the effect of great peace will come of itself."
translations.idiomatic: When censorate officials are due for promotion, let their performance be judged solely on the quantity and quality of their memorials. Then censorial officials will speak plainly, ordinary officials will have no cause to overstep their posts, and the ban on speaking out of turn will become unnecessary—peace will follow of itself.]

sentences.zh: 帝責其沽名，命貶一秩。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed him for seeking reputation and ordered demotion by one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accused him of courting reputation and ordered his rank reduced by one step.

sentences.zh: 科道合救，不允。

translations.literal: The censorate jointly interceded; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officials jointly petitioned for his pardon, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 庶偕同列胡時麟、梅國樓、郭顯忠復交章論劾，乃再降一秩，為湖廣按察司經歷。

translations.literal: Shu together with colleagues Hu Shilin, Mei Guolou, and Guo Xianzhong again submitted linked memorials in protest; Maohui was then demoted another rank and made commissioner of the Huguang Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, together with colleagues Hu Shilin, Mei Guolou, and Guo Xianzhong, submitted further linked memorials in protest, whereupon Maohui was demoted another rank and appointed commissioner of the Huguang Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部主事，以憂歸，屢薦不起。

translations.literal: He served as principal officer in the Ministry of Rites; he returned on mourning; repeatedly recommended, he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as principal officer in the Ministry of Rites, then returned home for mourning; though repeatedly recommended, he refused to resume office.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年，始起故官。

translations.literal: At home twenty years; then he was first raised to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for twenty years before being recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 進南京兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He advanced to director in the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，終太仆少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, he ended as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he ended his career as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 李沂，字景魯，嘉魚人。

translations.literal: Li Yi, style Jinglu, was a native of Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, styled Jinglu, came from Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fourteenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year he was granted Supervising Secretary in the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixteenth year he was appointed supervising secretary in the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 中官張鯨掌東廠，橫肆無憚。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhang Jing controlled the Eastern Depot and was overbearing without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhang Jing controlled the Eastern Depot and acted with unchecked arrogance.

sentences.zh: 御史何出光劾鯨死罪八，並及其黨錦衣都督劉守有、序班邢尚智。

translations.literal: Censor He Chuguang impeached Jing with eight capital crimes, also reaching his faction Elder Guard Commander Liu Shouyou and Orderly Xing Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Censor He Chuguang impeached Zhang Jing on eight capital charges and also implicated his allies, Elder Guard Commander Liu Shouyou and orderly Xing Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 尚智論死，守有除名，鯨被切讓，而任職如故。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was sentenced to death; Shouyou was stripped of name; Jing received sharp rebuke, yet held his post as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shangzhi was sentenced to death, Liu Shouyou was stripped of rank, and Zhang Jing received a stern rebuke, yet remained in office as before.

sentences.zh: 御史馬象乾復劾鯨，詆執政甚力，帝下象乾詔獄。

translations.literal: Censor Ma Xiangqian again impeached Jing, reviling the chief ministers with great force; the emperor sent Xiangqian to the imperial prison by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ma Xiangqian again impeached Zhang Jing, denouncing the chief ministers with unusual force, and the emperor sent Xiangqian to the imperial prison by edict.

sentences.zh: 大學士申時行等力救，且封還禦批，不報。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing and others forcefully interceded and also returned the imperial rescript sealed; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing and others interceded forcefully and even returned the imperial rescript sealed, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 許國、王錫爵復各申救，乃寢前命，而鯨竟不罪。

translations.literal: Xu Guo and Wang Xijue each again interceded; the previous order was then shelved, yet Jing ultimately was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guo and Wang Xijue each interceded again, and the earlier order was set aside, yet Zhang Jing was never punished.

sentences.zh: 外議謂鯨以金寶獻帝獲免。

translations.literal: Outside discussion held that Jing escaped by presenting gold and jewels to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Public rumor held that Zhang Jing escaped punishment by presenting gold and jewels to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 沂拜官甫一月，上疏曰：「陛下往年罪馮保，近日逐宋坤，鯨惡百保而萬坤，奈何獨濡忍不去？

translations.literal: Yi had held office only one month when he submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty in past years punished Feng Bao; recently you expelled Song Kun. Jing's evil is a hundred times Bao's and ten thousand times Kun's—why alone show indulgent tolerance and not remove him?
translations.idiomatic: Yi had held office barely a month when he submitted a memorial: [Your Majesty punished Feng Bao in earlier years and recently expelled Song Kun. Zhang Jing's wickedness exceeds Bao's a hundredfold and Kun's ten thousandfold—why show indulgence to him alone and leave him in place?

sentences.zh: 若謂其侍奉多年，則壞法亦多年；

translations.literal: If one says he has served many years, then he has also broken the law for many years;
translations.idiomatic: If one says he has served many years, then he has broken the law for just as many;

sentences.zh: 謂痛加省改，猶足供事，則未聞可馴虎狼使守門戶也。

translations.literal: if one says he has been severely corrected through pain and is still enough to serve—then one has never heard of taming tigers and wolves to guard the gate and household.
translations.idiomatic: if one says he has been sternly corrected and is still fit to serve, I have never heard of taming tigers and wolves to guard one's gate.

sentences.zh: 流傳鯨廣獻金寶，多方請乞，陛下猶豫，未忍斷決。

translations.literal: It circulates that Jing widely offered gold and jewels and begged in many ways; Your Majesty hesitates and has not yet borne to decide firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor spreads that Zhang Jing has lavished gold and jewels upon the court and begged through many channels, while Your Majesty hesitates and cannot bear to decide.

sentences.zh: 中外臣民，初未肯信，以為陛下富有四海，豈愛金寶；

translations.literal: Inside and outside, officials and people at first were unwilling to believe it, thinking Your Majesty possesses all within the four seas—how could you love gold and jewels;
translations.idiomatic: At first officials and commoners within and without the court refused to believe it, thinking Your Majesty owns all within the four seas—how could you covet gold and jewels;

sentences.zh: 威如雷霆，豈徇請乞。

translations.literal: your authority is like thunder—how could you yield to begging.
translations.idiomatic: your authority is like thunder—how could you yield to pleading.

sentences.zh: 及見明旨許鯨策勵供事，外議藉藉，遂謂為真。

translations.literal: When they saw the clear edict permitting Jing to exert himself in service, outside talk swarmed, and then they took it as true.
translations.idiomatic: But when they saw the explicit edict allowing Zhang Jing to continue in office with encouragement, public talk swelled, and people then took the rumor for truth.

sentences.zh: 虧損聖德，夫豈淺甚！

translations.literal: Impairment of sacred virtue—can it be slight!
translations.idiomatic: The damage to Your Majesty's virtue—can it be called slight!

sentences.zh: 且鯨奸謀既遂，而國家之禍將從此始，臣所大懼也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, once Jing's wicked scheming succeeds, the state's disaster will from this begin—that is what your minister greatly fears."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, once Zhang Jing's wicked designs succeed, the state's calamity will begin here—and that is what your servant most dreads.

sentences.zh: 是日，給事中唐堯欽亦具疏諫。

translations.literal: That day, Supervising Secretary Tang Yaoqin also fully memorialized in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: ] That same day, Supervising Secretary Tang Yaoqin also submitted a full memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝獨手沂疏，震怒，謂沂欲為馮保、張居正報仇，立下詔獄嚴鞫。

translations.literal: The emperor alone took Yi's memorial, stunned with rage, saying Yi wished to avenge Feng Bao and Zhang Juzheng; immediately he sent him to the imperial prison for strict interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor singled out Yi's memorial, flew into a rage, and declared that Yi sought to avenge Feng Bao and Zhang Juzheng; he immediately sent him to the imperial prison for harsh interrogation.

sentences.zh: 時行等乞宥，不從。

translations.literal: Shixing and others begged pardon; this was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing and the others pleaded for leniency, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 讞上，詔廷杖六十，斥為民。

translations.literal: When the case was reported up, an edict ordered sixty blows at court and dismissal as commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When the verdict was submitted, an edict ordered sixty blows at court and his dismissal to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 禦批至閣，時行等欲留禦批，中使不可，持去。

translations.literal: The imperial rescript reached the Grand Secretariat; Shixing and others wished to retain the rescript; the palace messenger would not allow it and took it away.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial rescript reached the Grand Secretariat, Shixing and the others tried to withhold it, but the palace messenger refused and carried it away.

sentences.zh: 帝特遣司禮張誠出監杖。

translations.literal: The emperor specially dispatched Directorate of Ceremonial's Zhang Cheng to go out and oversee the beating.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially dispatched Zhang Cheng of the Directorate of Ceremonial to supervise the beating in person.

sentences.zh: 時行等上疏，俱詣會極門候進止。

translations.literal: Shixing and others submitted memorials; all went to the Gate of Gathering of Ultimate to await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing and the others submitted memorials and all went to the Gate of Gathering of Ultimate to await the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 帝言：「沂置貪吏不言，而獨謂朕貪，謗誣君父，罪不可宥。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yi spoke of greedy officials not at all, yet alone said I am greedy—slandering and falsely accusing the sovereign and father; the crime cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: [Yi says nothing of corrupt officials, yet accuses me alone of greed—slandering and falsely accusing his sovereign and father; the crime cannot be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 竟杖之。

translations.literal: In the end he was beaten.
translations.idiomatic: ] In the end the beating was carried out.

sentences.zh: 太常卿李尚智、給事中薛三才等抗章論救，俱不報。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Minister Li Shangzhi, Supervising Secretary Xue Sancai, and others submitted forceful memorials interceding; all went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Minister Li Shangzhi, Supervising Secretary Xue Sancai, and others submitted forceful memorials in his defense, but all went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 國、錫爵以言不見用，引罪乞歸。

translations.literal: Guo and Xijue, their words not being used, took blame and begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guo and Wang Xijue, finding their remonstrance ignored, accepted blame and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 錫爵言：「廷杖非正刑，祖宗雖間一行之，亦未有詔獄、廷杖並加於一人者。

translations.literal: Xijue said: "Court beating is not orthodox punishment; the imperial ancestors though occasionally applied it, never also combined imperial prison and court beating on one person.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue said: [Court beating is not orthodox punishment. Though the imperial ancestors occasionally applied it, never before have imperial imprisonment and court beating both been imposed on one man.

sentences.zh: 故事，惟資賊大逆則有打問之旨，今豈可加之言官。」

translations.literal: By precedent, only when treason and rebellion reach capital crime is there an order for beating interrogation—how can this now be applied to censorial officials?"
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, beating interrogation was reserved for capital treason and rebellion. How can it now be applied to censorial officials?

sentences.zh: 帝優詔慰留錫爵，卒不聽其言。

translations.literal: The emperor with a gracious edict comforted and retained Xijue; ultimately he did not heed his words.
translations.idiomatic: ] The emperor issued a gracious edict comforting Xijue and keeping him in office, but in the end paid no heed to his words.

sentences.zh: 初，馮保獲罪，實鯨為之，故帝雲然。

translations.literal: At first, when Feng Bao was condemned, in fact Jing did it—hence the emperor spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, Feng Bao's downfall had in fact been Zhang Jing's doing, which is why the emperor spoke as he did.

sentences.zh: 或謂鯨罪不至如保。

translations.literal: Some said Jing's crime did not reach Bao's level.
translations.idiomatic: Some held that Zhang Jing's offenses did not equal Feng Bao's.

sentences.zh: 張誠掌司禮，素德保，授意言者發之，事秘莫能明也。

translations.literal: Zhang Cheng controlled the Directorate of Ceremonial, always regarded Bao with gratitude, and directed memorialists to raise it—the matter was secret and none could clarify it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng, who controlled the Directorate of Ceremonial, had long felt indebted to Feng Bao and prompted memorialists to raise the matter; the affair remained secret and none could fully clarify it.

sentences.zh: 其時，周弘禴、潘士藻皆以忤鯨得罪，而沂禍為烈。

translations.literal: At that time, Zhou Hongxi and Pan Shizao both offended Jing and were punished, but Yi's calamity was most severe.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhou Hongxi and Pan Shizao both offended Zhang Jing and were punished, but Li Yi suffered the harshest fate.

sentences.zh: 家居十八年，未召而卒。

translations.literal: At home eighteen years; before recall he died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for eighteen years and died before being recalled.

sentences.zh: 光宗嗣位，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded, he was posthumously given Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong succeeded to the throne, Li Yi was posthumously granted vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 弘禴，字元孚，麻城人。

translations.literal: Hongxi, style Yuanfu, was a native of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxi, styled Yuanfu, came from Macheng.

sentences.zh: 倜儻負奇，好射獵。

translations.literal: Unconventional and bearing extraordinary talent; fond of archery and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: He was free-spirited and unconventional, and loved archery and hunting.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷二年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the second year of Wanli and was appointed principal officer in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Wanli reign and was appointed principal officer in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 降無為州同知，遷順天通判。

translations.literal: He was demoted to assistant prefect of Wuwei and transferred to assistant prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to assistant prefect of Wuwei, then transferred to assistant prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，上疏指斥朝貴，言：「兵部尚書張學顏被論屢矣。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year he submitted a memorial denouncing court nobles, saying: "Minister of War Zhang Xueyan has been impeached many times already.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year he submitted a memorial denouncing court grandees: [Minister of War Zhang Xueyan has been impeached many times already.

sentences.zh: 陛下以學顏故，逐一給事中、三御史，此人心所共憤也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty for Xueyan's sake dismissed supervising secretaries and three censors one by one—this is what people's hearts commonly rage at.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for Xueyan's sake Your Majesty has dismissed supervising secretaries and three censors one after another—this is what all hearts condemn.

sentences.zh: 學顏結張鯨為兄弟，言官指論學顏而不敢及鯨，畏其勢耳。

translations.literal: Xueyan bonded with Zhang Jing as sworn brothers; censorial officials pointed at Xueyan but did not dare reach Jing—merely fearing his power.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan swore brotherhood with Zhang Jing, and censorial officials criticize Xueyan yet dare not touch Jing—merely because they fear his power.

sentences.zh: 若李植之論馮保，似乎忠讜矣，實張宏門客樂新聲為謀主。

translations.literal: Take Li Zhi's indictment of Feng Bao—it seems loyal and forthright, but in fact Zhang Hong's household retainer Yue Xinsheng was the mastermind.
translations.idiomatic: Take Li Zhi's attack on Feng Bao—it seems loyal and outspoken, but in truth the real strategist was Yue Xinsheng, a retainer in Zhang Hong's household.

sentences.zh: 其巡按順天，納娼為小妻，猖狂幹紀，則恃宏為內援也。

translations.literal: When he toured and inspected Shuntian, he took a prostitute as a minor wife and violated discipline with reckless abandon—this was because he relied on Hong as inside support.
translations.idiomatic: When he served as touring inspector of Shuntian, he took a prostitute as a concubine and brazenly violated discipline—all because he relied on Zhang Hong for support within the palace.

sentences.zh: 鯨、宏既竊陛下權，而植又竊司禮勢，此公論所不容。

translations.literal: Jing and Hong have already usurped Your Majesty's authority, and Zhi has usurped the Directorate of Ceremonial's power—this public opinion cannot tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing and Zhang Hong have already usurped Your Majesty's authority, and Li Zhi has usurped the power of the Directorate of Ceremonial—this is what public opinion cannot abide.

sentences.zh: 《祖訓》，大小官許至御前言事。

translations.literal: The Ancestral Instructions permit officials great and small to speak on affairs before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Ancestral Instructions permit officials of every rank to speak on affairs before the throne.

sentences.zh: 今吏科都給事中齊世臣乃請禁部曹建言。

translations.literal: Now Qi Shichen, Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section, asks to forbid department officials from offering counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qi Shichen, chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Section, now asks to forbid department officials from offering counsel.

sentences.zh: 曩居正竊權，臺省群頌功德，而首發其奸者，顧在艾穆、沈思孝，部曹言事果何負於國哉？

translations.literal: Formerly when Juzheng usurped power, the censorate and provincial offices together praised his merits and virtues, yet those who first exposed his wickedness were none other than Ai Mu and Shen Sixiao—what wrong have department officials who speak on affairs really done to the state?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng usurped power in the past, the censorate and provincial offices together praised his merits, yet those who first exposed his treachery were none other than Ai Mu and Shen Sixiao—what harm have department officials who speak on affairs really done the state?

sentences.zh: 居正惡員外郎管誌道之建白也，御史龔懋賢因誣以老疾；

translations.literal: Juzheng hated Section Vice-Director Guan Zhidao's forthright proposals, so Censor Gong Maoxian falsely charged him with age and illness;
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng hated the forthright proposals of section vice-director Guan Zhidao, so censor Gong Maoxian falsely charged him with age and illness;

sentences.zh: 惡主事趙世卿之條奏也，尚書王國光遂錮以王官。

translations.literal: he hated Principal Officer Zhao Shiqing's itemized memorials, and Minister Wang Guoguang thereupon confined him to a princely post.
translations.idiomatic: he hated the itemized memorials of principal officer Zhao Shiqing, and Minister Wang Guoguang thereupon confined him to a princely appointment.

sentences.zh: 論者切齒，為其附權奸而棄直言，長壅蔽之禍也。

translations.literal: Critics gnashed their teeth, for it attached to the power-holding villain and abandoned forthright speech, prolonging the disaster of obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Critics gnashed their teeth, for by siding with the power-holding villain and abandoning forthright speech they prolonged the disaster of obstruction.

sentences.zh: 今學顏、植交附鯨、宏，鯨敢竊柄，世臣豈不聞？

translations.literal: Now Xueyan and Zhi fraternize with and attach themselves to Jing and Hong; Jing dares to usurp the handle of power—has Shichen not heard?
translations.idiomatic: Now Xueyan and Zhi have attached themselves to Jing and Hong, and Jing dares to usurp real power—has Shichen not heard of this?

sentences.zh: 已不敢言，奈何反欲人不言乎？

translations.literal: He already dares not speak—how then can he turn around and wish that others not speak?
translations.idiomatic: He already dares not speak himself—how then can he turn around and wish that others not speak?

sentences.zh: 前此長吏垣者周邦傑、秦耀。

translations.literal: Before this, those who headed the Personnel Section were Zhou Bangjie and Qin Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the heads of the Personnel Section were Zhou Bangjie and Qin Yao.

sentences.zh: 當居正時，耀則甘心獵犬，邦傑則比跡寒蟬。

translations.literal: During Juzheng's time, Yao willingly served as hunting hound, while Bangjie took the winter cicada as his model.
translations.idiomatic: During Juzheng's time, Yao willingly served as a hunting hound, while Bangjie modeled himself on the winter cicada.

sentences.zh: 今耀官太常，邦傑官太仆矣，諫職無補，坐陟京卿，尚謂臺省足恃乎？

translations.literal: Now Yao holds office as Minister of Ceremonies and Bangjie as Minister of the Imperial Stud; they were useless in remonstrance duties yet were seated in metropolitan minister posts—is the censorate still held to be reliable?
translations.idiomatic: Now Yao is minister of ceremonies and Bangjie minister of the imperial stud—useless in their remonstrance duties, yet promoted to metropolitan ministerial posts—and you still say the censorate can be relied upon?

sentences.zh: 而乃禁諸臣言事也。

translations.literal: And yet he would forbid all officials from speaking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: And yet he would forbid all officials from speaking on affairs.

sentences.zh: 夫逐一人之言者其罪小，禁諸臣之言者其罪大。

translations.literal: To drive away one man's speech—the crime is small; to forbid all officials' speech—the crime is great.
translations.idiomatic: To drive away one man's speech is a small crime; to forbid all officials from speaking is a great one.

sentences.zh: 往者嚴嵩及居正猶不敢明立此禁，何世臣無忌憚一至此哉！

translations.literal: In the past Yan Song and even Juzheng did not dare openly establish this prohibition—how has Shichen become so utterly without restraint!
translations.idiomatic: In the past even Yan Song and Zhang Juzheng did not dare openly establish such a prohibition—how has Shichen become so utterly without restraint!

sentences.zh: 乞放學顏、植歸裏，出耀、邦傑於外，屏張鯨使閑居，而奪世臣諫職，嚴敕司禮張誠等止掌內府禮儀，毋幹政事，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: I beg that Xueyan and Zhi be released to return home, that Yao and Bangjie be sent outside, that Zhang Jing be removed to idle living, that Shichen be stripped of his remonstrance post, and that Zhang Cheng and others of the Directorate of Ceremonial be strictly charged to manage only inner-palace ritual and not meddle in state affairs—the realm would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Xueyan and Zhi be sent home, that Yao and Bangjie be posted outside, that Zhang Jing be removed to idle retirement, that Shichen be stripped of his remonstrance post, and that Zhang Cheng and others of the Directorate of Ceremonial be strictly ordered to manage only inner-palace ritual and not meddle in state affairs—the realm would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫代州判官，再遷南京兵部主事。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted him to magistrate of Daizhou, then transferred him again to principal officer in the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: ] The emperor was angry and demoted him to magistrate of Daizhou, then transferred him again to principal officer in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十七年，帝始倦勤，章奏多留中不下。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the emperor first grew weary of diligence; memorials were often kept within and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the emperor first grew weary of governing; memorials were often kept within and never answered.

sentences.zh: 弘禴疏諫，且請早建皇儲，不報。

translations.literal: Hongxi memorialized in remonstrance and also asked that the heir apparent be established early; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongxi memorialized in remonstrance and also asked that the heir apparent be established early, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 尋召為尚寶丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Seal Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as vice director of the Imperial Seal Office.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，命監察御史閱視寧夏邊務。

translations.literal: The next winter, he was ordered as Investigating Censor to inspect border affairs in Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was appointed investigating censor to inspect border affairs in Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 巡撫僉都御史梁問孟、巡茶御史鐘化民，取官帑銀交際，弘禴疏發之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator and Vice Censor-in-Chief Liang Wenmeng and Tea-Route Censor Zhong Huamin took treasury silver for social exchange; Hongxi exposed this in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator and vice censor-in-chief Liang Wenmeng and tea-route censor Zhong Huamin had taken official treasury silver for private exchange; Zhou Hongxi exposed them in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔褫問孟職，調化民於外。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Wenmeng of his post and transferred Huamin outside.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Liang Wenmeng of his post and transferred Zhong Huamin to an outside appointment.

sentences.zh: 河東有秦、漢二壩，弘禴請以石為之，浚渠北達鴛鴦諸湖，大興水利。

translations.literal: East of the river were the Qin and Han dams; Hongxi asked that they be rebuilt in stone, that channels be dredged north to reach the Mandarin Duck lakes and others, and that waterworks be greatly developed.
translations.idiomatic: East of the river stood the Qin and Han dams; Zhou Hongxi proposed rebuilding them in stone, dredging channels north to the Mandarin Duck lakes and beyond, and greatly expanding irrigation works.

sentences.zh: 還朝，以將材薦哱承恩、土文秀、哱雲。

translations.literal: On returning to court, he recommended Bo Chengen, Tu Wenxiu, and Bo Yun for military talent.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, he recommended Bo Chengen, Tu Wenxiu, and Bo Yun as men of military talent.

sentences.zh: 明年，承恩等反，坐謫澄海典史。

translations.literal: The next year Chengen and the others rebelled; on that account he was demoted to recorder of Chenghai.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Chengen and the others rebelled, and Zhou Hongxi was demoted to recorder of Chenghai on that account.

sentences.zh: 投劾歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: He submitted his resignation and returned home, dying there.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his resignation and returned home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，以嘗請建儲，贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, because he had once asked to establish the heir, he was posthumously given Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, because he had once asked that the heir be established, he was posthumously granted vice minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 潘士藻，字去華，婺源人。

translations.literal: Pan Shizao, style Quhua, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shizao, styled Quhua, came from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授溫州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，巡視北城。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor and inspected the North City.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor and assigned to inspect the North City.

sentences.zh: 慈寧宮近侍侯進忠、牛承忠私出禁城，狎婦女。

translations.literal: Palace attendants Hou Jinzhong and Niu Chengzhong of Cining Palace privately left the forbidden city and dallied with women.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants Hou Jinzhong and Niu Chengzhong of Cining Palace had left the forbidden city without permission and were dallying with women.

sentences.zh: 邏者執之，為所毆，訴於士藻。

translations.literal: Patrolmen seized them but were beaten by them; they appealed to Shizao.
translations.idiomatic: Patrolmen seized them but were beaten in the struggle and appealed to Pan Shizao.

sentences.zh: 私牒司禮監治之。

translations.literal: He privately sent a note to the Directorate of Ceremonial to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: He privately sent a note to the Directorate of Ceremonial asking that they be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝恚曰：「東廠何事？

translations.literal: The emperor, angry, said: "What business is the Eastern Depot?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angry, said: [What business is the Eastern Depot?

sentences.zh: 乃自外庭發。」

translations.literal: Yet this was initiated from the outer court."
translations.idiomatic: Yet this was initiated from the outer court.

sentences.zh: 杖兩閹，斃其一。

translations.literal: He had the two eunuchs beaten; one died.
translations.idiomatic: ] He had the two eunuchs beaten, and one died.

sentences.zh: 鯨方掌東廠，怒。

translations.literal: Jing was then in charge of the Eastern Depot and was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing was then in charge of the Eastern Depot and was furious.

sentences.zh: 會火災修省，士藻言：「今天下之患，莫大於君臣之意不通。

translations.literal: When a fire prompted self-examination, Shizao said: "Today's calamity under Heaven is nowhere greater than the failure of ruler and ministers to understand one another.
translations.idiomatic: When a fire prompted court self-examination, Pan Shizao said: [Today's greatest calamity under Heaven is the failure of ruler and ministers to understand one another.

sentences.zh: 宜仿祖制，及近時平臺暖閣召對故事，面議所當施罷。

translations.literal: One should follow ancestral institutions and the recent precedents of audience at the Level Platform and Warm Pavilion, and face to face discuss what should be enacted or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should follow ancestral institutions and the recent precedents of audience at the Level Platform and Warm Pavilion, and discuss face to face what should be enacted or abolished.

sentences.zh: 撤大工以俟豐歲，蠲織造、燒造以昭儉德，免金花額外征以佐軍食。

translations.literal: Withdraw great works to await abundant years; remit weaving and kiln manufacture to display frugal virtue; exempt extra levies of gold-flower silver to supplement military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Suspend major construction until years of plenty; remit weaving and kiln manufacture to display frugal virtue; exempt extra levies of gold-flower silver to supplement military provisions.

sentences.zh: 且時召講讀諸臣，問以經史。

translations.literal: Moreover, summon the lecturing and reading officials from time to time and question them on the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, summon the lecturing and reading officials from time to time and question them on the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 對賢人君子之時多，自能以敬易肆，以義奪欲。

translations.literal: When one faces worthy men and gentlemen often, one can naturally replace laxity with reverence and overcome desire with righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When one spends more time with worthy men and gentlemen, one can naturally replace laxity with reverence and overcome desire with righteousness.

sentences.zh: 修省之實，無過於此。」

translations.literal: The substance of self-examination goes no further than this."
translations.idiomatic: The substance of true self-examination goes no further than this.

sentences.zh: 鯨乃激帝怒，謫廣東布政司照磨。

translations.literal: Jing then stirred the emperor's anger, and he was demoted to aide in the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: ] Zhang Jing then stirred the emperor's anger, and Pan Shizao was demoted to aide in the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 科道交章論救，不聽。

translations.literal: Censorial officials submitted linked memorials pleading for him; this was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials submitted linked memorials pleading for him, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 尋擢南京吏部主事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to principal officer in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to principal officer in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚寶卿，卒官。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Director of the Imperial Seal Office and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to director of the Imperial Seal Office and died in office.

sentences.zh: 雒於仁，字少涇，涇陽人。

translations.literal: Luo Yuren, style Shaojing, was a native of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuren, styled Shaojing, came from Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 父遵，吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: His father Zun was Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun was chief supervising secretary of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 神宗初即位，馮保竊權。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor first succeeded to the throne, Feng Bao usurped power.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shenzong Emperor first succeeded to the throne, Feng Bao usurped power.

sentences.zh: 帝御殿，保輒侍側。

translations.literal: When the emperor held court, Bao always attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor held court, Feng Bao always stood at his side.

sentences.zh: 遵言：「保一侍從之仆，乃敢立天子寶座，文武群工拜天子邪，抑拜中官邪？

translations.literal: Zun said: "Bao is only a serving attendant—how dare he stand beside the Son of Heaven's throne? Do the civil and military officials bow to the Son of Heaven, or to a palace eunuch?
translations.idiomatic: Zun said: [Feng Bao is only a serving attendant—how dare he stand beside the Son of Heaven's throne? Do the civil and military officials bow to the Son of Heaven, or to a palace eunuch?

sentences.zh: 欺陛下幼沖，無禮至此！」

translations.literal: He deceives Your Majesty in youth and tender years—such lack of propriety to this point!"
translations.idiomatic: He takes advantage of Your Majesty's youth—such impudence has never been seen!

sentences.zh: 遵乃大學士高拱門生。

translations.literal: Zun was a disciple of Grand Secretary Gao Gong.
translations.idiomatic: ] Zun was a disciple of Grand Secretary Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 保疑遵受拱指，遂謀逐拱。

translations.literal: Bao suspected Zun had received Gong's direction and thereupon plotted to drive Gong out.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bao suspected that Zun had acted at Gao Gong's direction and thereupon plotted to drive Gong out.

sentences.zh: 遵疏留中。

translations.literal: Zun's memorial was kept within.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's memorial was kept within and never answered.

sentences.zh: 尋劾兵部尚書譚綸，因薦海瑞。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Minister of War Tan Lun and on that occasion recommended Hai Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he impeached Minister of War Tan Lun and on that occasion recommended Hai Rui.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書楊博稱綸才，詆瑞迂滯，疏遂寢。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Yang Bo praised Lun's talent and reviled Rui as pedantic and obstructive; the memorial was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Yang Bo praised Tan Lun's talent and reviled Hai Rui as pedantic and obstructive, and the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 頃之，綸陪祀日壇，咳不止。
