translations.literal: Shortly after, Lun attended sacrifice at the Sun Altar and could not stop coughing.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Tan Lun attended sacrifice at the Sun Altar and could not stop coughing.

sentences.zh: 御史景嵩、韓必顯劾綸衰病。

translations.literal: Censors Jing Song and Han Bixian impeached Lun for decline and illness.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Jing Song and Han Bixian impeached Tan Lun for decline and illness.

sentences.zh: 居正素善綸，而馮保欲緣是為遵罪，因傳旨詰嵩、必顯欲用何人代綸，令會遵推舉，遵等惶懼不敢承。

translations.literal: Juzheng had long been on good terms with Lun, but Feng Bao wished to use this to make a crime of Zun; he therefore transmitted an order questioning Song and Bixian as to whom they wished to use to replace Lun, and ordered them to meet with Zun to recommend someone—Zun and the others were fearful and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng had long been on good terms with Tan Lun, but Feng Bao wished to use this to make a crime of Zun; he therefore transmitted an order questioning Jing Song and Han Bixian as to whom they wished to use to replace Lun, and ordered them to meet with Zun to recommend someone—Zun and the others were fearful and dared not comply.

sentences.zh: 俱貶三秩，調外。

translations.literal: All were demoted three ranks and transferred outside.
translations.idiomatic: All were demoted three ranks and transferred to outside appointments.

sentences.zh: 遵得浙江布政司照磨。

translations.literal: Zun received aide in the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was given the post of aide in the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 保敗，屢遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: When Bao fell, he was repeatedly transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: After Feng Bao's fall, he was repeatedly promoted, eventually reaching director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 改右僉都御史，巡撫四川。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Censor-in-Chief on the right and Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice censor-in-chief on the right and grand coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 罷歸，卒。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and returned home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 於仁舉萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: Yuren passed the jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuren passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知肥鄉、清豐二縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Feixiang and Qingfeng counties, with benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as magistrate of Feixiang and Qingfeng, where his benevolent administration won praise.

sentences.zh: 十七年，入為大理寺評事。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he entered service as Evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he entered service as evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 疏獻四箴以諫。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial presenting Four Admonitions in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial presenting his Four Admonitions in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: Its summary says:
translations.idiomatic: Its summary reads:

sentences.zh: 臣備官歲餘，僅朝見陛下者三。

translations.literal: Your minister has held office more than a year and has seen Your Majesty at court only three times.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has held office for more than a year and has seen Your Majesty at court only three times.

sentences.zh: 此外惟聞聖體違和，一切傳免。

translations.literal: Apart from this, one hears only that the sacred person is unwell and that everything is passed along as exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from this, one hears only that Your Majesty's health is unwell and that all duties are passed along as exemptions.

sentences.zh: 郊祀廟享遣官代行，政事不親，講筵久輟。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice and temple offerings are dispatched through substitute officials; state affairs are not handled in person, and the lecture hall has long been suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice and temple offerings are performed by substitute officials; state affairs are not handled in person, and the lecture hall has long been suspended.

sentences.zh: 臣知陛下之疾，所以致之者有由也。

translations.literal: Your minister knows that Your Majesty's illness has causes by which it was brought about.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant knows that Your Majesty's illness has causes by which it was brought about.

sentences.zh: 臣聞嗜酒則腐腸，戀色則伐性，貪財則喪誌，尚氣則戕生。

translations.literal: Your minister has heard that fondness for wine rots the intestines, attachment to beauty wastes the nature, greed for wealth destroys the will, and esteem for temper harms life.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that fondness for wine rots the intestines, attachment to beauty wastes one's nature, greed for wealth destroys the will, and indulgence in temper harms life.

sentences.zh: 陛下八珍在禦，觴酌是耽，卜晝不足，繼以長夜。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has the eight delicacies at the imperial table and is devoted to cups and goblets; counting the daylight is not enough, and the long night follows.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has the eight delicacies at the imperial table and is devoted to cups and goblets; daylight drinking is not enough, and the revelry continues through the long night.

sentences.zh: 此其病在嗜酒也。

translations.literal: This is an illness whose seat is fondness for wine.
translations.idiomatic: This is an illness whose root is fondness for wine.

sentences.zh: 寵「十俊」以啟幸門，溺鄭妃，靡言不聽。

translations.literal: Favoring the "Ten Handsome Men" to open the gate of favor, drowning in Consort Zheng—no word of hers is not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Favoring the "Ten Handsome Men" to open the gate of favor, drowning in Consort Zheng—no word of hers goes unheeded.

sentences.zh: 忠謀擯斥，儲位久虛。

translations.literal: Loyal counsel is cast aside, and the heir's place has long stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal counsel is cast aside, and the heir's place has long stood empty.

sentences.zh: 此其病在戀色也。

translations.literal: This is an illness whose seat is attachment to beauty.
translations.idiomatic: This is an illness whose root is attachment to beauty.

sentences.zh: 傳索帑金，括取幣帛。

translations.literal: Orders are transmitted demanding treasury gold; silks and cloth are seized and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Orders are transmitted demanding treasury gold; silks and cloth are seized and gathered.

sentences.zh: 甚且掠問宦官，有獻則已，無則譴怒。

translations.literal: So far as to plunder and interrogate palace eunuchs—if there is an offering it stops; if not, there is rebuke and rage.
translations.idiomatic: So far as to plunder and interrogate palace eunuchs—if there is an offering it stops; if not, there is rebuke and rage.

sentences.zh: 李沂之瘡痍未平，而張鯨之貲賄復入。

translations.literal: The wounds of Li Yi's case had not yet healed, yet Zhang Jing's bribes entered again.
translations.idiomatic: The wounds of Li Yi's case had not yet healed, yet Zhang Jing's bribes entered the palace again.

sentences.zh: 此其病在貪財也。

translations.literal: This is an illness whose seat is greed for wealth.
translations.idiomatic: This is an illness whose root is greed for wealth.

sentences.zh: 今日榜宮女，明日抶中官，罪狀未明，立斃杖下。

translations.literal: Today palace women are posted for punishment; tomorrow palace eunuchs are beaten—the crimes are not yet clear, yet they are immediately beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Today palace women are posted for punishment; tomorrow palace eunuchs are beaten—the crimes are not yet clear, yet they are immediately beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 又宿怨藏怒於直臣，如範俊、姜應麟、孫如法輩，皆一詘不申，賜環無日。

translations.literal: Moreover, old grudges and hidden anger are stored against forthright officials such as Fan Jun, Jiang Yinglin, Sun Rufa, and the like—all have suffered one defeat without redress, and the day of restored office is nowhere in sight.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, old grudges and hidden anger are stored against forthright officials such as Fan Jun, Jiang Yinglin, and Sun Rufa—all have suffered one defeat without redress, and the day of restored office is nowhere in sight.

sentences.zh: 此其病在尚氣也。

translations.literal: This is an illness whose seat is esteem for temper.
translations.idiomatic: This is an illness whose root is indulgence in temper.

sentences.zh: 四者之病，膠繞身心，豈藥石所可治？

translations.literal: These four illnesses cling to body and mind—how can drugs and stones cure them?
translations.idiomatic: These four illnesses cling to body and mind—how can drugs and stones cure them?

sentences.zh: 今陛下春秋鼎盛，猶經年不朝，過此以往，更當何如？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is in the prime of life, yet for years has not held court—beyond this, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty is in the prime of life, yet for years has not held court—beyond this, what then?

sentences.zh: 孟軻有取於法家拂士，今鄒元標其人也。

translations.literal: Mencius took something from Legalist renegade scholars; today Zou Yuanbiao is such a man.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius valued the renegade scholars who dared to oppose power; today Zou Yuanbiao is such a man.

sentences.zh: 陛下棄而置之，臣有以得其故矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty casts him aside and leaves him unused—your minister has grounds for knowing the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty casts him aside and leaves him unused—your servant has grounds for knowing the reason.

sentences.zh: 元標入朝，必首言聖躬，次及左右。

translations.literal: When Yuanbiao enters court, he always speaks first of the sacred person, next of those at Your Majesty's side.
translations.idiomatic: When Zou Yuanbiao enters court, he always speaks first of Your Majesty's person, next of those at Your Majesty's side.

sentences.zh: 是以明知其賢，忌而弗用。

translations.literal: Therefore, though knowing his worth, one resents and does not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, though knowing his worth, Your Majesty resents him and will not employ him.

sentences.zh: 獨不思直臣不利於陛下，不便於左右，深有利於宗社哉！

translations.literal: Will you alone not reflect that forthright officials are not advantageous to Your Majesty and not convenient to those at your side, yet are deeply advantageous to the ancestral altars?
translations.idiomatic: Will Your Majesty not reflect that forthright officials may be inconvenient to you and to those at your side, yet are deeply advantageous to the altars of state?

sentences.zh: 陛下之溺此四者，不曰操生殺之權，人畏之而不敢言，則曰居邃密之地，人莫知而不能言。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's drowning in these four things—if one does not say you hold the power of life and death and men fear you and dare not speak, then one says you dwell in deep seclusion and men do not know and cannot speak.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's drowning in these four things—if one does not say you hold the power of life and death and men fear you and dare not speak, then one says you dwell in deep seclusion and men do not know and cannot speak.

sentences.zh: 不知鼓鐘於宮，聲聞於外，幽獨之中，指視所集。

translations.literal: One does not know that when drums and bells sound in the palace, the sound is heard outside; in solitary seclusion, pointing and gazing converge.
translations.idiomatic: One does not know that when drums and bells sound in the palace, the sound is heard outside; even in solitary seclusion, every glance and whisper converge upon you.

sentences.zh: 且保祿全軀之士可以威權懼之，若懷忠守義者，即鼎鋸何避焉！

translations.literal: Moreover, those who preserve salary and keep their bodies whole may be frightened by authority and power; but those who harbor loyalty and uphold righteousness—what need they fear even the cauldron and saw!
translations.idiomatic: Those who care only for their stipends and their skins may be cowed by power—but a man who holds loyalty and righteousness in his heart has nothing to fear from torture or death.

sentences.zh: 臣今敢以四箴獻。

translations.literal: Your servant now dares to offer four admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant now dares to present four admonitions.

sentences.zh: 若陛下肯用臣言，即立誅臣身，臣雖死猶生也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty is willing to use my words, even if you immediately execute my person, though I die I would still live.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will heed what I say, then even if you have me executed on the spot, I shall die and yet live on.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下垂察。

translations.literal: Only I pray Your Majesty will look down and examine.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this with care.

sentences.zh: 酒箴曰：耽彼麹蘗，昕夕不輟。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Wine says: Indulging in that yeast and malt, from dawn to dusk without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Admonition on Wine reads: Drowning in ferment and brew, from morning till night without pause.

sentences.zh: 心誌內懵，威儀外缺。

translations.literal: The mind and will grow dull within; dignity and ritual are lacking without.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit dulls within, and dignity and decorum fail without.

sentences.zh: 神禹疏狄，夏治興隆。

translations.literal: Divine Yu kept wine at a distance, and Xia's governance flourished and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Yu kept his distance from wine, and the rule of Xia flourished.

sentences.zh: 進藥陛下，醲醑勿崇。

translations.literal: A medicine offered to Your Majesty: do not exalt thick brew.
translations.idiomatic: A remedy I offer Your Majesty: do not elevate strong drink.

sentences.zh: 色箴曰：艷彼妖姬，寢興在側。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Pleasure says: Those dazzling seductresses, at waking and at rest ever at your side.
translations.idiomatic: The Admonition on Pleasure reads: Those bewitching women, at your waking and at your sleeping ever at your side.

sentences.zh: 啟寵納侮，爭妍誤國。

translations.literal: Opening favor invites contempt; vying for beauty ruins the state.
translations.idiomatic: Bestowing favor invites contempt; rivalry for beauty brings ruin to the realm.

sentences.zh: 成湯不邇，享有遐壽。

translations.literal: Tang of Shang kept no proximity to such things, and enjoyed long life.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang kept no such company and enjoyed a long reign.

sentences.zh: 進藥陛下，內嬖勿厚。

translations.literal: A medicine offered to Your Majesty: do not thickly favor inner intimates.
translations.idiomatic: A remedy I offer Your Majesty: do not lavish favor on inner favorites.

sentences.zh: 財箴曰：「競彼镠鐐，錙銖必盡。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Wealth says: "Racing after that gold and silver, not a shu or zhu is spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Admonition on Wealth reads: "Scrambling after gold and silver, not the smallest coin is left untouched.

sentences.zh: 公帑稱盈，私家懸罄。

translations.literal: The public treasury is said to be full, yet private households are utterly empty.
translations.idiomatic: The public coffers are said to overflow, while private homes are stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 武散鹿臺，八百歸心。

translations.literal: Wu dispersed the treasures of Lutai, and the eight hundred lords returned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu opened the stores of Lutai, and the lords of the realm gave him their hearts.

sentences.zh: 隋煬剝利，天命難諶。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui scraped for profit, and Heaven's mandate was hard to retain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui scraped for every profit, and Heaven's mandate slipped from his grasp.

sentences.zh: 進藥陛下，貨賄勿侵。

translations.literal: A medicine offered to Your Majesty: do not encroach on goods and bribes.
translations.idiomatic: A remedy I offer Your Majesty: do not reach for wealth and graft.

sentences.zh: 氣箴曰：逞彼忿怒，恣睢任情。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Anger says: Giving free rein to rage, arrogant and wilful as one pleases.
translations.idiomatic: The Admonition on Anger reads: Unleashing wrath, arrogant and wilful, following every impulse.

sentences.zh: 法尚操切，政盩公平。

translations.literal: Law should be strict yet tempered; governance should be even and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Law ought to be firm yet measured; government ought to be steady and just.

sentences.zh: 虞舜溫恭，和以致祥。

translations.literal: Yu Shun was gentle and respectful; harmony brought forth auspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shun was mild and courteous, and harmony brought forth blessings.

sentences.zh: 秦皇暴戾，群怨孔彰。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin was violent and cruel; popular resentment was manifest everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin was savage and cruel, and popular hatred showed plainly on every side.

sentences.zh: 進藥陛下，舊怨勿藏。

translations.literal: A medicine offered to Your Majesty: do not hoard old grievances.
translations.idiomatic: A remedy I offer Your Majesty: do not harbor old resentments.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝震怒。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor was shaken with rage.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 會歲暮，留其疏十日。

translations.literal: It happened to be year's end; he kept the memorial for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: It chanced to be year's end, and he kept the memorial for ten days.

sentences.zh: 所雲「十俊」，蓋十小閹也。

translations.literal: What it called the "Ten Worthies" were in fact ten petty eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called "Ten Worthies" were in truth ten low-ranking eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 明年正旦，召見閣臣申時行等於毓德宮，手於仁疏授之。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day the following year, he summoned Grand Secretaries including Shen Shixing to the Yude Palace and handed them Yu Ren's memorial in person.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day the following year, he summoned Grand Secretaries including Shen Shixing to the Yude Palace and personally handed them Yu Ren's memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝自辨甚悉，將置之重典。

translations.literal: The Emperor defended himself at great length and was about to impose the severest penalties.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebutted the charges at length and was about to impose the harshest punishment.

sentences.zh: 時行等委曲慰解，見帝意不可回，乃曰：「此疏不可發外，恐外人信以為真。

translations.literal: Shen and the others gently comforted and reasoned with him; seeing the Emperor's mind could not be turned, they said: "This memorial must not be released outside, lest outsiders take it as truth.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and the others gently soothed and reasoned with him; seeing that the Emperor's mind could not be moved, they said, "This memorial must not be circulated outside the court, lest outsiders take it for truth.

sentences.zh: 願陛下曲賜優容，臣等即傳諭寺卿，令於仁去位可也。」

translations.literal: We beg Your Majesty graciously to show forbearance; we shall immediately relay instructions to the Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship to have Yu Ren leave his post, and that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to show gracious forbearance; we shall at once instruct the Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship to have Yu Ren leave his post, and that will suffice.

sentences.zh: 帝乃頷之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 居數日，於仁引疾，遂斥為民。

translations.literal: After several days Yu Ren cited illness and was dismissed, reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Yu Ren pleaded illness and was dismissed, reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Ceremonial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director of the Ceremonial Guard.

sentences.zh: 馬經綸，字主一，順天通州人。

translations.literal: Ma Jinglun, courtesy name Zhuyi, was a native of Tongzhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jinglun, styled Zhuyi, was a native of Tongzhou in Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除肥城知縣，入為御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Feicheng, then entered service as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Feicheng, then entered the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 二十三年冬，兵部考選軍政。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-third year, the Ministry of War conducted its evaluation and selection for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-third year, the Ministry of War conducted its evaluation and selection for military appointments.

sentences.zh: 帝謂中有副千戶者，不宜擅署四品職。

translations.literal: The Emperor said that among those selected was an assistant chiliarch, who should not have been arbitrarily assigned a fourth-rank post.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said that among those selected was an assistant chiliarch, who ought not to have been assigned a fourth-rank post on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 責部臣徇私，兵科不糾發。

translations.literal: He blamed the ministry officials for favoritism and the military section of the Office of Scrutiny for failing to expose it.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed the ministry officials for showing favoritism and the military section of the Office of Scrutiny for failing to expose the matter.

sentences.zh: 降武選郎韓範、都給事中吳文梓雜職。

translations.literal: He demoted Han Fan, Military Selection Officer, and Wu Wenzu, Supervising Secretary, to miscellaneous posts.
translations.idiomatic: He demoted Han Fan, Military Selection Officer, and Wu Wenzu, Supervising Secretary, to miscellaneous posts.

sentences.zh: 鐫員外郎曾偉芳、主事江中信、程僖、陳楚產、給事中劉仕瞻三秩，調極邊。

translations.literal: He cut three ranks from Outside Department Secretary Zeng Weifang, Directors Jiang Zhongxin, Cheng Xi, and Chen Chuchan, and Supervising Secretary Liu Shizhan, and transferred them to the farthest borders.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped three ranks from Outside Department Secretary Zeng Weifang, Directors Jiang Zhongxin, Cheng Xi, and Chen Chuchan, and Supervising Secretary Liu Shizhan, and posted them to the remotest frontier.

sentences.zh: 以御史區大倫、俞價、強思、給事中張同德言事常忤旨，亦鐫三秩。

translations.literal: Because Censors Ou Dalun, Yu Jia, and Qiang Si and Supervising Secretary Zhang Tongde often offended the throne in their remonstrances, he likewise cut three ranks from each.
translations.idiomatic: Because Censors Ou Dalun, Yu Jia, and Qiang Si and Supervising Secretary Zhang Tongde often offended the throne in their memorials, he likewise stripped three ranks from each.

sentences.zh: 而五城御史夏之臣、朱鳳翔、塗喬遷、時偕行、楊述中籍中官客用家，不稱旨，並謫邊遠典史。

translations.literal: The Five-Office censors Xia Zhichen, Zhu Fengxiang, Tu Qiaoqian, Shi Xiexing, and Yang Shuzhong relied on Ke Yong's household as clients of the inner eunuchs and failed to please the throne; all were relegated to distant district secretary posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Five-Office censors Xia Zhichen, Zhu Fengxiang, Tu Qiaoqian, Shi Xiexing, and Yang Shuzhong had relied on the household of Ke Yong, a client of the inner eunuchs, and failed to please the throne; all were relegated to distant district secretary posts.

sentences.zh: 又以客用貲財匿崇信伯費甲金家，刑部拷訊無實，謫郎中徐維濂於外。

translations.literal: Because Ke Yong's funds were suspected of being hidden in the home of Baron Fei Jiajin of Chongxin, and torture under the Ministry of Justice produced no proof, Section Director Xu Weilian was relegated outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ke Yong's funds were suspected of being hidden in the home of Baron Fei Jiajin of Chongxin, and interrogation under torture by the Ministry of Justice found no proof, Section Director Xu Weilian was relegated outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 一時嚴旨頻下，且不得千戶主名，舉朝震駭。

translations.literal: For a time severe edicts rained down one after another, and because the name of the chiliarch was never disclosed, the whole court was shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: For a time harsh edicts poured down in succession, and because the name of the chiliarch was never disclosed, the whole court was shaken with alarm.

sentences.zh: 時東廠太監張誠失帝意。

translations.literal: At the time the Eastern Depot eunuch Zhang Cheng had fallen from imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Eastern Depot eunuch Zhang Cheng had fallen from imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 誠家奴錦衣副千戶霍文炳當遷指揮僉事，部臣先已奏請，而帝欲尋端罪言官，遂用是為罪。

translations.literal: Zhang's household slave Huo Wenbing, an assistant chiliarch in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, was due for promotion to Assistant Commandant; the ministry had already memorialized the request, but the Emperor sought a pretext to punish the remonstrating officials and used this as the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's household slave Huo Wenbing, an assistant chiliarch in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, was due for promotion to Assistant Commandant; the ministry had already memorialized the appointment, but the Emperor sought a pretext to punish the remonstrating officials and used this as the charge.

sentences.zh: 旋移怒兩京科道，以為緘默，命掌印者盡鐫三秩。

translations.literal: He soon shifted his wrath to the supervising secretaries and censors of both capitals, charging them with silence, and ordered those holding the seals to cut three ranks from each.
translations.idiomatic: He soon turned his wrath on the supervising secretaries and censors of both capitals, charging them with silence, and ordered those holding the seals to strip three ranks from each.

sentences.zh: 於是給事中耿隨龍、鄒廷彥、黎道昭、孫羽侯、黃運泰、毛一公，御史李宗延、顧際明、袁可立、綦才、吳禮嘉、王有功、李固本，南京給事中伍文煥、費必興、盧大中，御史柳佐、聶應科、李文熙等十九人俱調外，留者並停俸一年。

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretaries Geng Suilong, Zou Tingyan, Li Daozhao, Sun Yuhou, Huang Yuntai, and Mao Yigong; Censors Li Zongyan, Gu Jiming, Yuan Keli, Qi Cai, Wu Lijia, Wang Yougong, and Li Guben; Nanjing Supervising Secretaries Wu Wenhuan, Fei Bixing, and Lu Dazhong; and Censors Liu Zuo, Nie Yingke, and Li Wenxi—nineteen men in all—were transferred outside the capital, while those who remained all had their salaries suspended for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Supervising Secretaries Geng Suilong, Zou Tingyan, Li Daozhao, Sun Yuhou, Huang Yuntai, and Mao Yigong; Censors Li Zongyan, Gu Jiming, Yuan Keli, Qi Cai, Wu Lijia, Wang Yougong, and Li Guben; Nanjing Supervising Secretaries Wu Wenhuan, Fei Bixing, and Lu Dazhong; and Censors Liu Zuo, Nie Yingke, and Li Wenxi—nineteen men in all—were transferred outside the capital, while those who remained all had their salaries suspended for one year.

sentences.zh: 又令吏部列上職名，再罷御史馮從吾、薛繼茂、王慎德、姚三讓四人。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Ministry of Personnel to list names by rank and again dismissed Censors Feng Congwu, Xue Jimao, Wang Shende, and Yao Sanrang.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Ministry of Personnel to submit a list of names by rank and again dismissed Censors Feng Congwu, Xue Jimao, Wang Shende, and Yao Sanrang.

sentences.zh: 大學士趙誌臯、陳於陛、沈一貫及九卿各疏爭，尚書石星請罷職以寬諸臣，皆不納。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao, Chen Yubi, and Shen Yiguan and the Nine Ministers each submitted memorials contesting the decision; Minister Shi Xing asked to resign to obtain leniency for the officials, but none of this was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao, Chen Yubi, and Shen Yiguan and the Nine Ministers each submitted memorials in protest; Minister Shi Xing asked to resign in the hope of winning leniency for the officials, but none of it was accepted.

sentences.zh: 於陛又特疏申救。

translations.literal: Yu Bi submitted a separate memorial to intercede.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bi submitted a separate memorial to plead for them.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命降諸人雜職，悉調邊方。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angry and ordered the men demoted to miscellaneous posts and all transferred to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew angry and ordered the men demoted to miscellaneous posts and all transferred to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 尚書孫丕揚等以詔旨轉嚴，再疏乞宥。

translations.literal: Ministers Sun Piyang and others, seeing the edict grow ever harsher, memorialized again begging pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Sun Piyang and others, seeing the edict grow ever harsher, memorialized again begging for pardon.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，盡奪職為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew still angrier and stripped them all of office, reducing them to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew still angrier and stripped them all of office, reducing them to commoners.

sentences.zh: 經綸憤甚，抗疏曰：

translations.literal: Jinglun was deeply indignant and submitted a defiant memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jinglun was deeply indignant and submitted a defiant memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 頃屢奉嚴旨，斥逐南北言官。

translations.literal: Recently I have repeatedly received severe edicts expelling remonstrating officials north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have repeatedly received harsh edicts expelling remonstrating officials north and south.

sentences.zh: 臣幸蒙恩，罰俸供職，今日乃臣諫諍之日矣。

translations.literal: Your servant has been fortunate enough to receive grace, punished only with salary withheld while remaining at his post; today is the day for me to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has been fortunate enough to receive grace, punished only with salary withheld while remaining at his post; today is the day for me to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 陛下數年以來，深居靜攝，君臣道否，中外俱抱隱憂。

translations.literal: For several years Your Majesty has dwelt in deep seclusion and quiet withdrawal; the way between ruler and minister is blocked, and inside and outside the court alike harbor hidden worry.
translations.idiomatic: For several years Your Majesty has dwelt in deep seclusion; the bond between ruler and minister is broken, and court and country alike harbor hidden dread.

sentences.zh: 所恃言路諸臣，明目張膽為國家裁辨邪正，指斥奸雄。

translations.literal: What was relied upon were the officials of the remonstrance path, who with open eyes and bold hearts judged right and wrong for the state and denounced villains and usurpers.
translations.idiomatic: What the realm relied upon were the remonstrating officials, who with open eyes and bold hearts judged right and wrong for the state and denounced villains and usurpers.

sentences.zh: 雖廟堂處分，未必盡協輿論，而縉紳公議，頗足維持世風，此高廟神靈實鑒佑之。

translations.literal: Though decisions from the hall may not always accord with public opinion, the shared judgment of the gentry is quite enough to uphold the world's moral tone; the spirit of Grand Ancestor truly witnesses and blesses this.
translations.idiomatic: Though decisions from the throne may not always accord with public opinion, the shared judgment of the gentry is enough to uphold the moral tone of the age—and the spirit of Grand Ancestor truly witnesses and blesses this.

sentences.zh: 所資臺省耳目之用大矣，陛下何為一旦自塗其耳目邪？

translations.literal: The use of the Censorate and Secretariat as eyes and ears is so great—why should Your Majesty in a single day blind and stop up his own eyes and ears?
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate and Secretariat serve as eyes and ears of incomparable value—why should Your Majesty in a single day blind and stop up his own eyes and ears?

sentences.zh: 夫以兵部考察之故，而罪兵科是已。

translations.literal: To punish the military section of the Office of Scrutiny over the Ministry of War's evaluation would have been enough.
translations.idiomatic: To punish the military section of the Office of Scrutiny over the Ministry of War's evaluation would have been enough.

sentences.zh: 乃因而蔓及於他給事，又波連於諸御史。

translations.literal: Yet the matter spread to other supervising secretaries and rippled out to the various censors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the matter spread to other supervising secretaries and rippled outward to the various censors.

sentences.zh: 去者不明署其應得之罪，留者不明署其姑恕之由。

translations.literal: For those sent away, their deserving crimes were not clearly stated; for those who remained, the reasons for provisional leniency were not made clear.
translations.idiomatic: For those sent away, the crimes they deserved were never clearly stated; for those who remained, the reasons for provisional leniency were never made clear.

sentences.zh: 雖聖意淵微，未易窺測，而道路傳說，嘖有煩言。

translations.literal: Though the sage intent is profound and not easy to fathom, roadsides buzz with rumor and there is no lack of vexing talk.
translations.idiomatic: Though the sage intent is profound and not easy to fathom, rumor runs through the streets and vexing talk abounds.

sentences.zh: 陛下年來厭苦言官，動輒罪以瀆擾，今忽變而以箝口罪之。

translations.literal: In recent years Your Majesty has wearied of remonstrating officials and often punished them for irreverent disturbance; now suddenly the charge has changed to silencing their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Your Majesty has wearied of remonstrating officials and often punished them for irreverent disturbance; now suddenly the charge has changed to keeping silent.

sentences.zh: 夫以無言罪言官，言官何辭。

translations.literal: To punish remonstrators for saying nothing—what defense can remonstrators offer?
translations.idiomatic: To punish remonstrators for saying nothing—what defense can remonstrators offer?

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀陛下所為罪言官者，猶淺之乎罪言官也。

translations.literal: I privately observe that in punishing remonstrators, Your Majesty has still fallen short of punishing them as they deserve.
translations.idiomatic: I privately observe that in punishing remonstrators, Your Majesty has still not punished them as they deserve.

sentences.zh: 乃言官今日之箝口不言者，有五大罪焉。

translations.literal: For the remonstrators' present silence there are five great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: For the remonstrators' present silence there are five great crimes.

sentences.zh: 陛下不郊天有年矣，曾不能援故典排闥以諍，是陷陛下之不敬天者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has not performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven for many years, yet they never invoked precedent and forced the gate to remonstrate—thus implicating Your Majesty in disrespect for Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven for many years, yet they never invoked precedent and forced the gate to remonstrate—thus implicating Your Majesty in disrespect for Heaven.

sentences.zh: 罪一。

translations.literal: First crime.
translations.idiomatic: First crime.

sentences.zh: 陛下不享祖有年矣，曾不能開至誠牽裾以諍，是陷陛下之不敬祖者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has not offered sacrifice to the ancestors for many years, yet they never opened their utmost sincerity and clutched your robe to admonish—thus implicating Your Majesty in disrespect for the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not offered sacrifice to the ancestors for many years, yet they never opened their utmost sincerity and clutched your robe to admonish—thus implicating Your Majesty in disrespect for the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 罪二。

translations.literal: Second crime.
translations.idiomatic: Second crime.

sentences.zh: 陛下輟朝不禦，停講不舉，言官言之而不能卒復之，是陷陛下不能如祖宗之勤政。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ceased holding court and stopped the lecture hall, and though remonstrators spoke of it they could not in the end restore these practices—thus implicating Your Majesty in failing to match the ancestors' diligence in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ceased holding court and stopped the lecture hall, and though remonstrators spoke of it they could not in the end restore these practices—thus implicating Your Majesty in failing to match the ancestors' diligence in governance.

sentences.zh: 罪三。

translations.literal: Third crime.
translations.idiomatic: Third crime.

sentences.zh: 陛下去邪不決，任賢不篤，言官言之而不能強得之，是陷陛下不能如祖宗之用人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty removes the wicked without resolve and employs the worthy without steadfastness; remonstrators spoke of it but could not force the issue—thus implicating Your Majesty in failing to match the ancestors in employing men.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty removes the wicked without resolve and employs the worthy without steadfastness; remonstrators spoke of it but could not force the issue—thus implicating Your Majesty in failing to match the ancestors in employing men.

sentences.zh: 罪四。

translations.literal: Fourth crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth crime.

sentences.zh: 陛下好貨成癖，禦不少恩，肘腋之間，叢怨蓄變，言官俱慮之，而卒不能批鱗諫止，是陷陛下甘棄初政，而弗猶克終。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's craving for wealth has become a habit; His Majesty grants no sparing grace, and in the closest quarters grievances gather and change brews; all remonstrators feared this yet in the end could not risk the dragon's scales to stop it—thus implicating Your Majesty in willingly abandoning the early policies without achieving a good end.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's craving for wealth has become a habit; you grant no sparing grace, and in your closest quarters grievances gather and trouble brews; all remonstrators feared this yet in the end could not touch the dragon's scales to stop it—thus implicating Your Majesty in willingly abandoning the early policies without achieving a good end.

sentences.zh: 罪五。

translations.literal: Fifth crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth crime.

sentences.zh: 言官負此大罪，陛下肯奮然勵精而以五罪罪之，豈不當哉！

translations.literal: That remonstrators bear these great crimes—if Your Majesty would vigorously rouse himself and punish them with these five crimes, would that not be fitting!
translations.idiomatic: That remonstrators bear these great crimes—if Your Majesty would vigorously rouse yourself and punish them with these five crimes, would that not be fitting!

sentences.zh: 奈何責之箝口不言者，不於此而於彼也！

translations.literal: Yet why punish them for silencing their mouths on this matter and not on that!
translations.idiomatic: Yet why punish them for keeping silent here, and not for keeping silent there!

sentences.zh: 日者廷臣交章論救，不惟不肯還職，而且落職為民。

translations.literal: Recently court ministers submitted memorial after memorial in defense, yet not only were the dismissed not restored to office, they were reduced to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Recently court ministers submitted memorial after memorial in their defense, yet not only were the dismissed not restored to office—they were reduced to commoners.

sentences.zh: 夫諸臣本出草莽，今還初服，亦復何憾。

translations.literal: Those officials originally came from the wilds; now restored to plain dress, what regret need they have?
translations.idiomatic: Those officials originally came from humble life; now restored to plain dress, what regret need they have?

sentences.zh: 獨念朝廷之過舉不可遂，大臣之忠懇不可拂。

translations.literal: I reflect only that the court's mistaken acts must not be allowed to stand, and a great minister's loyal earnestness must not be brushed aside.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect only that the court's mistaken acts must not be allowed to stand, and a great minister's loyal earnestness must not be brushed aside.

sentences.zh: 陛下不聽閣疏之救，改降級而為雜職，則輔臣何顏？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will not heed the Grand Secretariat's intercession and change demotion to miscellaneous posts instead, what face can the chief ministers show?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not heed the Grand Secretariat's intercession and change demotion to miscellaneous posts instead, what face can the chief ministers show?

sentences.zh: 是自離其腹心也。

translations.literal: This is to part from one's own heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: This is to cut yourself off from your own heart and core.

sentences.zh: 不聽部疏之救，改雜職而為編氓，則九卿何顏？

translations.literal: If you will not heed the ministry's intercession and change miscellaneous posts to common status, what face can the Nine Ministers show?
translations.idiomatic: If you will not heed the ministry's intercession and change miscellaneous posts to common status, what face can the Nine Ministers show?

sentences.zh: 是自戕其股肱也。

translations.literal: This is to maim one's own arms and legs.
translations.idiomatic: This is to maim your own arms and legs.

sentences.zh: 夫君臣一體，元首雖明，亦賴股肱腹心耳目之用。

translations.literal: Ruler and minister are one body; though the head be bright, it still relies on the use of arms, legs, heart, belly, eyes, and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and minister are one body; though the head be bright, it still relies on its arms, legs, heart, core, eyes, and ears.

sentences.zh: 今乃自塞其耳目，自離其腹心，自戕其股肱，陛下將誰與共理天下事乎！

translations.literal: Now you stop up your own eyes and ears, part from your own heart and belly, maim your own arms and legs—with whom, Your Majesty, will you together govern the affairs of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Now you stop up your own eyes and ears, cut yourself off from your own heart and core, maim your own arms and legs—with whom, Your Majesty, will you govern the affairs of the realm!

sentences.zh: 夫人君受命於天，與人臣受命於君一也。

translations.literal: A ruler receives his mandate from Heaven just as a minister receives his mandate from his ruler.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler receives his mandate from Heaven just as a minister receives his mandate from his ruler.

sentences.zh: 言官本無大罪，一旦震怒，罪以失職，無一敢抗命者。

translations.literal: The remonstrators had no great crime; in a burst of wrath they were punished with loss of office, and not one dared resist the command.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrators had committed no great crime; in a burst of wrath they were punished with loss of office, and not one dared resist the command.

sentences.zh: 既大失人心，必上拂天意。

translations.literal: Having already lost the hearts of men greatly, this must surely go against Heaven's intent above.
translations.idiomatic: Having already lost the hearts of men, this must surely go against Heaven's intent above.

sentences.zh: 萬一上天震怒，以陛下之不郊不帝、不朝不講、不惜才、不賤貨，咎失人君之職，而赫然降非常之災，不知陛下爾時能抗天命否乎？

translations.literal: If by chance Heaven is shaken with wrath, charging that for failure to sacrifice at the suburbs, to perform the Di sacrifice, to hold court, to lecture, to cherish talent, and to disdain wealth Your Majesty has lost a ruler's duty, and sends down a manifest extraordinary calamity—at that time, can Your Majesty resist Heaven's mandate?
translations.idiomatic: If by chance Heaven is shaken with wrath, charging that for failing to sacrifice at the suburbs, to perform the Di sacrifice, to hold court, to lecture, to cherish talent, and to disdain wealth Your Majesty has lost a ruler's duty, and sends down a manifest extraordinary calamity—at that time, can Your Majesty resist Heaven's mandate?

sentences.zh: 臣不能抗君，君不能抗天，此理明甚，陛下獨不思自為社稷計乎？

translations.literal: Your servant cannot resist his ruler, nor can a ruler resist Heaven; this principle is abundantly clear—does Your Majesty alone refuse to think for the sake of the altars of state?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cannot resist his ruler, nor can a ruler resist Heaven; this principle is abundantly clear—does Your Majesty alone refuse to think for the sake of the altars of state?

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，亦貶三秩，出之外。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and likewise cut three ranks from him and sent him outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly angered and likewise stripped three ranks from him and sent him outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 經綸既獲譴，工科都給事中海陽林熙春等上疏曰：「陛下怒言官緘默，斥逐三十余人，臣等不勝悚懼。

translations.literal: After Jinglun had been punished, Supervising Secretaries of the Office of Works including Lin Xichun of Haiyang submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty was angered that remonstrators kept silent and expelled more than thirty men; we cannot overcome our dread and fear.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinglun had been punished, Supervising Secretaries of the Office of Works including Lin Xichun of Haiyang submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty was angered that remonstrators kept silent and expelled more than thirty men; we are overcome with dread and fear.

sentences.zh: 今御史經綸慷慨陳言，竊意必溫旨褒嘉，顧亦從貶斥。

translations.literal: Now Censor Jinglun spoke forthrightly and passionately; we privately thought he would surely receive a gracious edict of praise, yet he too was demoted and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Now Censor Jinglun spoke forthrightly and passionately; we privately thought he would surely receive a gracious edict of praise, yet he too was demoted and expelled.

sentences.zh: 是以建言罪邪，抑以不言罪邪？

translations.literal: Is the crime speaking out, or is the crime not speaking?
translations.idiomatic: Is the crime speaking out, or is the crime not speaking?

sentences.zh: 臣等不能解也。

translations.literal: We your servants cannot understand it.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot make sense of it.

sentences.zh: 前所罪者，既以不言之故，今所罪者又以敢言之故，令臣等安所適從哉？

translations.literal: Those punished before were condemned for not speaking; those punished now are condemned for daring to speak—where are we your servants to turn?
translations.idiomatic: Those punished before were condemned for keeping silent; those punished now are condemned for daring to speak—how are we to know what to do?

sentences.zh: 陛下誠以不言為溺職，則臣等不難進憂危之苦詞；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly holds silence to be dereliction of duty, then we your servants would not find it hard to offer bitter words of worry and peril;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly holds silence to be dereliction of duty, we would not hesitate to speak the bitter truths of worry and peril;

sentences.zh: 誠以直言為忤旨，則臣等不難效喑默之成習。

translations.literal: if frank speech is truly held to offend the imperial will, then we your servants would not find it hard to follow the settled habit of mute silence.
translations.idiomatic: if frank speech is truly held to offend the imperial will, we would just as readily fall back into the settled habit of mute silence.

sentences.zh: 但恐廟堂之上，率諂佞取容，非君上之福也。

translations.literal: We only fear that above in the hall of state all will follow flattery and sycophancy to win favor—and that is no blessing for the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: We only fear that the court will fill with flatterers and sycophants seeking favor—and that can bring the sovereign no good.

sentences.zh: 臣等富貴榮辱之念豈與人殊，然寧為此不為彼者，毋亦沐二百余年養士之恩，不負君父，且不負此生耳。

translations.literal: Are we your servants' thoughts of wealth, honor, glory, and disgrace any different from other men's? Yet that we would choose this and not that is perhaps because we have bathed in more than two hundred years of the grace by which scholars are nurtured—we would not fail our ruler and father, and would not fail this life of ours.
translations.idiomatic: Our thoughts of wealth, honor, and disgrace are no different from anyone else's. Yet we choose to speak out rather than stay silent because we have received more than two hundred years of imperial nurture for scholars—we owe it to our ruler and to our own lives not to fail in our duty.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何深怒痛疾，而折辱至是哉！」

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty be so deeply angered and pained, and humiliate us to this extent!"
translations.idiomatic: Why must Your Majesty be so deeply enraged and humiliate us to this degree!"

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，謫熙春茶鹽判官，加貶經綸為典史。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew still angrier. Xichun was demoted to judicial administrator of tea and salt; Jinglun was further demoted to archivist.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew still angrier. Xichun was demoted to judicial administrator of tea and salt, and Jinglun was further reduced to archivist.

sentences.zh: 熙春遂引疾去。

translations.literal: Xichun thereupon resigned, citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Xichun thereupon resigned, citing illness.

sentences.zh: 是日，御史定興鹿久徵等亦上疏，請與諸臣同罪，貶澤州判官。

translations.literal: That same day, Censor Lu Jiuzheng of Dingxing and others also submitted a memorial asking to share the same punishment as the other officials, and were demoted to judicial administrators of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, Censor Lu Jiuzheng of Dingxing and others also submitted a memorial asking to share the other officials' punishment and were demoted to judicial administrators of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 二疏列名凡數十人，悉奪俸。

translations.literal: The two memorials listed names totaling several dozen men in all, and all had their salaries suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The two memorials named several dozen men in all, and all had their salaries suspended.

sentences.zh: 頃之，南京御史東莞林培疏陳時政。

translations.literal: Before long, Nanjing Censor Lin Pei of Dongguan submitted a memorial setting forth current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Nanjing Censor Lin Pei of Dongguan submitted a memorial on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝追怒經綸，竟斥為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor, still angry at Jinglun, ultimately banished him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, still angry at Jinglun, ultimately stripped him of office and banished him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 既歸，杜門卻掃凡十年。

translations.literal: After he returned home, he shut his doors and swept away visitors for ten years in all.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home, he shut his doors to the world and lived in seclusion for ten years.

sentences.zh: 卒，門人私謚聞道先生。

translations.literal: When he died, his disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master Who Heard the Way.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master Who Heard the Way.

sentences.zh: 培由鄉舉為新化知縣。

translations.literal: Pei, through the provincial examination, became magistrate of Xinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Pei entered office through the provincial examination and became magistrate of Xinhua.

sentences.zh: 縣僻陋，廣置社學教之。

translations.literal: The county was remote and poor; he broadly established community schools to teach the people.
translations.idiomatic: The county was remote and backward, so he established community schools throughout it to educate the people.

sentences.zh: 民有死於盜者，不得。

translations.literal: When a commoner died at the hands of robbers, the case could not be solved.
translations.idiomatic: When a commoner was killed by robbers, the culprits could not be found.

sentences.zh: 禱於神，隨蝴蝶所至獲盜，時驚為神。

translations.literal: He prayed to the spirit and, following wherever the butterflies went, captured the robber; people at the time marveled at it as divine.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed to the local deity and, following wherever butterflies flew, captured the robber; people at the time marveled at it as a miracle.

sentences.zh: 征授南京御史，劾罪誠意伯劉世延，置其爪牙於法。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Nanjing Censor, impeached Marquis Liu Shiyan of Chengyi, and brought his henchmen to justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Nanjing Censor, impeached Marquis Liu Shiyan of Chengyi, and brought his henchmen to justice.

sentences.zh: 已，上書言徐維濂不當謫；

translations.literal: Later he submitted a memorial saying Xu Weilian should not have been demoted;
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted a memorial arguing that Xu Weilian should not have been demoted;

sentences.zh: 陜西織花絨、購回青擾民，宜罷；

translations.literal: that Shaanxi's weaving of flowered velvet and purchasing of huiqing blue pigment harassed the people and should be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: that Shaanxi's production of flowered velvet and procurement of huiqing blue pigment harassed the people and should be stopped;

sentences.zh: 湖廣以魚鲊、江南以織造並奪撫按官俸，蘇州通判至以織造故褫官，皆不可訓；

translations.literal: that Huguang withheld the salaries of surveillance and grand coordinators over fish paste, and Jiangnan did the same over weaving, and even the vice prefect of Suzhou was stripped of office on account of weaving—all of which set a bad example;
translations.idiomatic: that Huguang withheld provincial officials' salaries over fish paste levies, and Jiangnan did the same over weaving levies, until even the vice prefect of Suzhou was stripped of office for weaving matters—all of which set a ruinous example;

sentences.zh: 並論及沈思孝等。

translations.literal: and he also discussed Shen Sixiao and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed Shen Sixiao and others.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫福建鹽運知事。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered and demoted him to attendant of Fujian salt transport.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angered and demoted him to attendant of Fujian salt transport.

sentences.zh: 告歸，卒。

translations.literal: He asked to retire and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement, returned home, and died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，復經綸官，贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, Jinglun's office was restored and he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, Jinglun's office was restored and he was posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 培贈光祿少卿，熙春亦還故職。

translations.literal: Pei was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Xichun also had his former office restored.
translations.idiomatic: Pei was posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Xichun also had his former office restored.

sentences.zh: 屢遷大理卿，年老乞罷。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to President of the Court of Judicial Review; in old age he asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted until he became President of the Court of Judicial Review; in old age he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 時李宗延、柳佐輩鹹官於朝，頌其先朝建言事。

translations.literal: At the time Li Zongyan, Liu Zuo, and their like all held office at court and praised his remonstrances in the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Zongyan, Liu Zuo, and others then in office at court praised his remonstrances under the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 詔加戶部右侍郎，致仕。

translations.literal: An edict added the title of Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue, and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue, and he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 劉綱，邛州人。

translations.literal: Liu Gang was a man of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gang was a native of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖文恂，孝子。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wen Xun was a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wen Xun was renowned for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 父應辰，舉鄉試，不仕，亦以孝義聞。

translations.literal: His father Yingchen passed the provincial examination but did not take office, and was also known for filial piety and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingchen passed the provincial examination but declined office and was also known for filial piety and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 綱舉萬歷二十三年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: Gang passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-third year of Wanli and was made a Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Gang passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-third year of Wanli and was appointed a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 二十五年七月，上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year, he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 去歲兩宮災，詔示天下，略無禹、湯罪己之誠，文、景蠲租之惠，臣已知天心之未厭矣。

translations.literal: Last year the two palaces burned; the edict issued to the realm showed scarcely the sincerity with which Yu and Tang blamed themselves, or the grace with which Wen and Jing remitted rents—I your servant already knew that Heaven's heart was not yet satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the two palaces burned, yet the edict issued to the realm showed scarcely the self-reproach of Yu and Tang or the rent remissions of Wen and Jing—I knew then that Heaven was not yet appeased.

sentences.zh: 比大工肇興，伐木榷稅，采石運瓷，遠者萬里，近者亦數百里。

translations.literal: When the great works began, timber was felled and monopoly taxes levied, stone was quarried and porcelain transported—those coming from afar traveled ten thousand li, and even those nearby several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When major construction began, timber was felled and monopoly taxes levied, stone quarried and porcelain transported—supplies came from as far as ten thousand li away, and even nearby sources lay several hundred li distant.

sentences.zh: 小民竭膏血不足供費，絕筋骨不足任勞，鬻妻子不能償貸。

translations.literal: Common people exhausted their flesh and blood yet could not meet the costs, broke sinew and bone yet could not bear the labor, and sold wives and children yet could not repay their debts.
translations.idiomatic: Common people drained their flesh and blood yet could not meet the costs, broke their bodies with labor yet could not finish the work, and sold wives and children yet still could not repay their debts.

sentences.zh: 加以旱魃為災，野無青草，人情胥怨，所在如仇。

translations.literal: Added to this, the drought demon brought calamity; the fields had no green grass; human hearts all resented, and everywhere men were like enemies.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this came drought; the fields withered bare of green grass, resentment spread everywhere, and men looked on one another as enemies.

sentences.zh: 而天下悔禍，三殿復災。

translations.literal: Yet when the realm repented its calamities, the Three Halls burned again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even as the realm repented its calamities, the Three Halls burned again.

sentences.zh: 《五行志》曰：「君不思道，厥災燒宮。」

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Elements says: "When the ruler does not reflect on the Way, the calamity is the burning of the palace."
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Five Elements says, "When the ruler does not reflect on the Way, the calamity is the burning of the palace."

sentences.zh: 陛下試自省，晝之為、夜之息，思在道乎，不在道乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, try to examine yourself: in what you do by day and in what you rest from by night, is your thought upon the Way, or not upon the Way?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, examine yourself: in what you do by day and in what you rest from by night, are your thoughts on the Way, or not?

sentences.zh: 凡敬天法祖，親賢遠奸，寡欲保身，賤貨慎德，俱謂之道，反是非道矣。

translations.literal: Revering Heaven and honoring the ancestors, drawing close to the worthy and keeping the wicked at a distance, limiting desires and preserving the person, disdaining wealth and guarding virtue—all these are called the Way; their opposites are not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Revering Heaven and honoring the ancestors, drawing close to the worthy and keeping the wicked at a distance, limiting desires and preserving oneself, disdaining wealth and guarding virtue—all these are the Way; their opposites are not.

sentences.zh: 陛下比年以來，簡禋祀，罷朝講，棄股肱，閡耳目，斷地脈，忽天象，君臣有數載之隔，堂陛若萬里而遙。

translations.literal: In recent years Your Majesty has simplified sacrificial rites, abolished court lectures, cast aside close ministers, blocked eyes and ears, cut the earth's veins, and ignored celestial signs—so that ruler and ministers have been separated for years, and hall and steps seem ten thousand li apart.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Your Majesty has simplified sacrificial rites, abolished court lectures, cast aside close ministers, blocked his eyes and ears, disturbed the earth's veins, and ignored celestial signs—so that ruler and ministers have been separated for years, and the throne seems ten thousand li from the court.

sentences.zh: 陛下深居靜攝，所為祈天永命者何狀，即外廷有不知，上天寧不見邪？

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells deep in seclusion and quiet restraint—what form do your acts of praying to Heaven for enduring mandate take? Even if the outer court does not know, would Heaven above not see?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dwells deep in seclusion—what form do your acts of praying to Heaven for enduring mandate take? Even if the outer court does not know, would Heaven above not see?

sentences.zh: 今日之災，其應以類，天若曰：皇之不極，於誰會歸，何以門為？

translations.literal: Today's calamity answers in kind; Heaven seems to say: the royal failure—upon whom should blame fall? What need is there for gates?
translations.idiomatic: Today's calamity answers in kind; Heaven seems to say: the royal failure—upon whom should blame fall? What need is there for gates?

sentences.zh: 朝儀久曠，於誰稟仰，何以殿為？

translations.literal: Court ceremony has long been neglected—upon whom do men look for guidance? What need is there for halls?
translations.idiomatic: Court ceremony has long been neglected—upon whom do men look for guidance? What need is there for halls?

sentences.zh: 元宰素餐，有汙政地，何以閣為？

translations.literal: The chief minister eats salary without work and has a place that defiles governance—what need is there for the Grand Secretariat?
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister draws salary without serving and has a place that defiles governance—what need is there for the Grand Secretariat?

sentences.zh: 其所以示警戒，勸更新者，至深切矣。

translations.literal: The warning shown and the urging to renew have been most profound.
translations.idiomatic: The warning shown and the urging to renew could not be more profound.

sentences.zh: 尚可因循玩愒，重怒上帝哉！

translations.literal: Can one still drift along in delay and idleness and again anger the Lord on High!
translations.idiomatic: How can one still drift along in delay and idleness and again anger the Lord on High!

sentences.zh: 臣聞五行之性，忌積喜暢。

translations.literal: I your servant have heard that the nature of the Five Elements hates accumulation and delights in release.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the nature of the Five Elements hates accumulation and delights in release.

sentences.zh: 積者，災之伏也，請冒死而言積之狀。

translations.literal: Accumulation is where calamity lies hidden; I beg to risk death and speak of the forms of accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulation is where calamity lies hidden; I beg leave to risk death and describe what has accumulated.

sentences.zh: 皇長子冠婚、冊立久未舉行，是曰積典。

translations.literal: The capping, marriage, and investiture of the heir apparent have long gone unperformed—this is called accumulated rites.
translations.idiomatic: The capping, marriage, and investiture of the heir apparent have long gone unperformed—this is accumulated ritual neglect.

sentences.zh: 大小臣僚以職事請，強半不報，是曰積牘。

translations.literal: Great and small officials submit business on their duties, yet more than half receive no reply—this is called accumulated documents.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small officials submit business on their duties, yet more than half receive no reply—this is accumulated paperwork.

sentences.zh: 外之司府有官無人，是曰積缺。

translations.literal: Outside, the offices have posts but no men—this is called accumulated vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital, offices have posts but no men to fill them—this is accumulated vacancy.

sentences.zh: 罪斥諸臣，概不錄敘，是曰積才。

translations.literal: Officials punished and expelled are on the whole not restored to service—this is called accumulated talent.
translations.idiomatic: Officials punished and expelled are on the whole not restored to service—this is accumulated talent wasted.

sentences.zh: 閫外有揚帆之醜，中原起揭竿之徒，是曰積寇。

translations.literal: Beyond the passes there are the shame of ships under sail, and in the Central Plain men rise with poles in hand—this is called accumulated bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the passes pirates sail with impunity, and in the Central Plain men rise in rebellion—this is accumulated disorder.

sentences.zh: 守邊治河，諸臣虛詞罔上，恬不為怪，是曰積玩。

translations.literal: In guarding the borders and managing the rivers, the officials offer empty words to deceive their superiors and are calmly unashamed—this is called accumulated negligence.
translations.idiomatic: In guarding the borders and managing the rivers, officials offer empty words to deceive their superiors and feel no shame—this is accumulated negligence.

sentences.zh: 諸所為積，陛下不能以明斷決，元輔趙誌臯不能以去就爭，天應隨之，毫髮不爽。

translations.literal: For all these accumulations, Your Majesty cannot decide them with clear judgment, and Chief Minister Zhao Zhigao cannot contend over staying or leaving—Heaven's response follows, not a hair's breadth astray.
translations.idiomatic: For all these accumulations, Your Majesty cannot resolve them with clear judgment, and Chief Minister Zhao Zhigao will not fight over staying or leaving—Heaven's response follows, not a hair's breadth astray.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不召九卿、臺諫面議得失，見兔顧犬，未為晚也。

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not summon the Nine Ministers and the remonstrating censors to discuss gains and losses face to face? When one sees the hare, then look to the hound—it is not yet too late.
translations.idiomatic: Why does Your Majesty not summon the Nine Ministers and the remonstrating censors to discuss affairs face to face? It is not yet too late to loose the hound when the hare appears.

sentences.zh: 若必專任誌臯，處堂相安，小之隳政事而羞士類，大之叢民怨而益大怒。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must rely solely on Zhigao, sitting at ease in the hall, in small matters he will ruin governance and shame the scholar class; in great matters he will heap up popular resentment and increase Heaven's wrath.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on relying solely on Zhigao, sitting at ease in the hall, in small matters he will ruin governance and shame the scholar class; in great matters he will heap up popular resentment and increase Heaven's wrath.

sentences.zh: 天下大計奈何以此匪人當之！

translations.literal: How can the great plan of the realm be entrusted to such a worthless man!
translations.idiomatic: How can the fate of the realm be entrusted to such a worthless man!

sentences.zh: 此不可令關白諸酋聞也。

translations.literal: This must not be allowed to reach the ears of the Jurchen chiefs of Guanbai.
translations.idiomatic: This must not be allowed to reach the ears of the Jurchen chiefs.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏，恚甚，將罪之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the memorial, he was furious and was about to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor received the memorial, he was furious and was about to punish him.

sentences.zh: 以方遘殿災，留中不報。

translations.literal: Because the palace had just suffered a fire, it was kept at court and no reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Because the palace had just suffered a fire, the memorial was kept at court and no reply was issued.

sentences.zh: 已而授編修。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 居二年，京察。

translations.literal: After two years came the capital evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: After two years came the capital evaluation.

sentences.zh: 坐浮躁，調外任，遂歸。

translations.literal: He was judged for being frivolous and impetuous, transferred to an outside post, and then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was judged for being frivolous and impetuous, transferred to an outside post, and then returned home.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died.

sentences.zh: 故事，翰林與政府聲氣相屬。

translations.literal: By precedent, the Hanlin Academy and the chief ministers were of one voice and one breath.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the Hanlin Academy and the chief ministers moved in concert.

sentences.zh: 綱直攻誌臯短，故嗛之不置，假察典中之。

translations.literal: Gang directly attacked Zhigao's faults, so he was resented without end and was got at through the evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Gang had directly attacked Zhigao's faults, so Zhigao resented him without end and got at him through the evaluation.

sentences.zh: 明世以庶吉士專疏建言者，前惟鄒智，後則劉之綸與綱，並四川人。

translations.literal: In the Ming dynasty, those Hanlin academicians who devoted memorials to remonstrance were, before, only Zou Zhi, and afterward Liu Zhilun and Gang—all men of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming dynasty, the Hanlin academicians who devoted themselves to memorial remonstrance were, earlier, only Zou Zhi, and later Liu Zhilun and Gang—all natives of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 戴士衡，字章尹，莆田人。

translations.literal: Dai Shiheng, styled Zhangyin, was a man of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shiheng, styled Zhangyin, was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 除新建知縣，擢吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xinjian, then promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Office of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Xinjian, then promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Office of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 薊州總兵官王保濫殺南兵，士衡極論其罪。

translations.literal: Wang Bao, regional commander of Jizhou, wantonly killed southern troops; Shiheng argued his crime to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao, regional commander of Jizhou, wantonly killed southern troops; Shiheng argued his crimes at length.

sentences.zh: 已，請亟補言官，劾石星誤國大罪五。

translations.literal: Later he asked that remonstrating officials be urgently replenished and impeached Shi Xing for five great crimes of harming the state.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked that remonstrating officials be urgently replenished and impeached Shi Xing on five great counts of harming the state.

sentences.zh: 山東稅使陳增請假便宜得舉刺將吏，淮、揚魯保亦請節制有司，士衡力爭。

translations.literal: Chen Zeng, tax commissioner of Shandong, asked leave to investigate and impeach generals and officials at his discretion; Lu Bao of Huai and Yang also asked to control civil officials—Shiheng contested this vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zeng, tax commissioner of Shandong, asked leave to investigate and impeach generals and officials at his discretion; Lu Bao of Huai and Yang also asked to control civil officials—Shiheng contested both vigorously.

sentences.zh: 仁聖太后梓宮發引，帝不親送，士衡言：「母子至情，送死大事，奈何於內庭數武地，靳一舉足勞。

translations.literal: When the coffin of Empress Dowager Rensheng was sent on its way, the Emperor did not escort it in person. Shiheng said: "The bond between mother and son is the deepest feeling; sending off the dead is a great matter—how can one, within the inner court over a distance of a few paces, begrudge the labor of a single step?
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin of Empress Dowager Rensheng was sent on its way, the Emperor did not escort it in person. Shiheng said, "The bond between mother and son is the deepest feeling in the world; sending off the dead is a grave duty—how can one, within the inner court over a distance of a few paces, begrudge the effort of a single step?

sentences.zh: 今山陵竣事，願陛下扶杖出迎神主，庶少慰聖母之靈，答臣民之望。」

translations.literal: Now that the imperial tomb is finished, I wish that Your Majesty would lean on a staff and go out to receive the spirit tablet, so as perhaps to give some comfort to the holy mother's spirit and answer the hopes of officials and people."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the imperial tomb is finished, I wish that Your Majesty would lean on a staff and go out to receive the spirit tablet, so as to give some comfort to the Empress Dowager's spirit and answer the hopes of officials and people."

sentences.zh: 錦衣千戶鄭一麟奏開昌平銀礦。

translations.literal: Battalion Commander Zheng Yilin of the Embroidered Uniform Guard memorialized to open the silver mine at Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion Commander Zheng Yilin of the Embroidered Uniform Guard memorialized to open the silver mine at Changping.

sentences.zh: 士衡以地逼天壽山，抗疏爭。

translations.literal: Shiheng, because the site lay close to Tianshou Mountain, submitted a forceful memorial in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng, because the site lay close to Tianshou Mountain, submitted a forceful memorial in opposition.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received a reply.
translations.idiomatic: None received a reply.

sentences.zh: 二十五年正月，極陳天下大計，言：「方今事勢不可知者三：天意也，人心也，氣運也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year, he set forth the great plan of the realm to the utmost, saying: "At present there are three things in the situation that cannot be known: Heaven's intent, the hearts of men, and the turn of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year, he set forth the great plan of the realm at length, saying, "At present there are three things in the situation that cannot be known: Heaven's intent, the hearts of men, and the turn of fortune.

sentences.zh: 大可慮者五：紀綱廢弛也，戎狄侵陵也，根本動搖也，武備疏略也，府藏殫竭也。

translations.literal: There are five things greatly to be feared: the laws and institutions lie in ruin, the barbarians invade and encroach, the foundations are shaken, military preparedness is neglected, and the treasury is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: There are five things greatly to be feared: the laws and institutions lie in ruin, the barbarians invade and encroach, the foundations are shaken, military preparedness is neglected, and the treasury is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 其切要而當亟正者一，則君心也。

translations.literal: There is one thing most urgent and needing immediate correction: the ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: There is one thing most urgent and needing immediate correction: the ruler's heart.

sentences.zh: 陛下高拱九重，目不睹師保之容，耳不聞丞弼之議，美麗當前，燕惰自佚，即欲殫聰明以計安社稷，其道無由。

translations.literal: Your Majesty sits high and withdrawn within the ninefold palace; your eyes do not behold the faces of tutors and guardians, your ears do not hear the deliberations of ministers and assistants; beauty lies before you, and in ease and idleness you give yourself to pleasure—even if you wished to exhaust your intelligence to plan the security of the altars of state, there would be no way to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sits high and withdrawn within the palace; your eyes do not behold the faces of tutors and guardians, your ears do not hear the deliberations of ministers and assistants; beauty lies before you, and in ease and idleness you give yourself to pleasure—even if you wished to exhaust your intelligence to secure the altars of state, there would be no way to do so.

sentences.zh: 誠宜時禦便殿，召執政大臣講求化理，則心清欲寡，政事自修。」

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to hold court from time to time in the side hall, summon the chief ministers to discuss the principles of transformation, and then the heart will be clear and desires few, and governance will right itself."
translations.idiomatic: It is truly fitting to hold court from time to time in the side hall, summon the chief ministers to discuss the principles of good governance, and then the heart will be clear and desires few, and governance will right itself."

sentences.zh: 亦不報。

translations.literal: This too received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: This too received no reply.

sentences.zh: 日本封事敗，再劾星及沈惟敬、楊方亨，且列上防倭八事。

translations.literal: When the investiture of Japan failed, he again impeached Shi Xing as well as Shen Weijing and Yang Fangheng, and also submitted eight measures for guarding against Japanese pirates.
translations.idiomatic: When the investiture of Japan failed, he again impeached Shi Xing as well as Shen Weijing and Yang Fangheng, and also submitted eight measures for guarding against Japanese pirates.

sentences.zh: 多議行。

translations.literal: Many of the proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 俄劾南京工部尚書葉夢熊、刑部侍郎呂坤、薊遼總督孫幰及通政參議李宜春。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached Ye Mengxiong, Minister of Works at Nanjing; Lu Kun, Vice Minister of Justice; Sun Han, Grand Coordinator of Jiliao; and Li Yichun, Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached Ye Mengxiong, Minister of Works at Nanjing; Lu Kun, Vice Minister of Justice; Sun Han, Grand Coordinator of Jiliao; and Li Yichun, Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 時幰已罷，宜春自引歸，坤亦以直諫去。

translations.literal: At the time Han had already been dismissed, Yichun had withdrawn on his own and returned home, and Kun had also left over frank remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Han had already been dismissed, Yichun had withdrawn and returned home on his own, and Kun had also left after frank remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉道亨右坤，力詆士衡，謂其受大學士張位指。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Daoheng sided with Kun and fiercely denounced Shiheng, saying he acted at the direction of Grand Secretary Zhang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Daoheng sided with Kun and fiercely denounced Shiheng, saying he acted at the direction of Grand Secretary Zhang Wei.

sentences.zh: 士衡亦劾道亨與星同鄉，為星報復。

translations.literal: Shiheng also impeached Daoheng as a fellow townsman of Shi Xing, acting in revenge for Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng also impeached Daoheng as a fellow townsman of Shi Xing, acting in revenge for Shi.

sentences.zh: 帝以言官互爭，皆報寢。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the remonstrating officials were quarreling with one another, shelved all the memorials without action.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, because the remonstrating officials were quarreling with one another, shelved all the memorials without action.

sentences.zh: 尋劾罷文選郎中白所知。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached and had dismissed Bai Suozhi, Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached and had dismissed Bai Suozhi, Director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 帝惡吏部郎，貶黜者二十二人，因詰責吏科朋比。

translations.literal: The Emperor hated the Ministry of Personnel directors; twenty-two were demoted and expelled, and he thereupon rebuked the Office of Personnel for factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hated the Ministry of Personnel directors; twenty-two were demoted and expelled, and he thereupon rebuked the Office of Personnel for factional collusion.

sentences.zh: 都給事中劉為楫、楊廷蘭、張正學、林應元及士衡俱引罪。

translations.literal: Chief Supervising Secretaries Liu Weiji, Yang Tinglan, Zhang Zhengxue, and Lin Yingyuan, together with Shiheng, all took blame upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Supervising Secretaries Liu Weiji, Yang Tinglan, Zhang Zhengxue, and Lin Yingyuan, together with Shiheng, all took blame upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 詔貶為楫一秩，與廷蘭等並調外。

translations.literal: An edict demoted Liu Weiji one rank, and together with Tinglan and the others he was transferred outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted Liu Weiji one rank and transferred him, along with Tinglan and the others, to posts outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 士衡得蘄州判官。

translations.literal: Shiheng received appointment as assistant magistrate of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng was appointed assistant magistrate of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 無何，詔改遠方，乃授陜西鹽課副提舉。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict changed his destination to a remote region, and he was appointed Deputy Salt-tax Intendant of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict reassigned him to a distant post, and he was made Deputy Salt-tax Intendant of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 未赴，會《憂危竑議》起，竟坐遣戍。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post, the affair of the "Youwei Jiong Memorial" arose, and he was ultimately sentenced to exile as a frontier guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, the affair of the "Youwei Jiong Memorial" erupted, and he was ultimately banished to frontier guard duty.

sentences.zh: 先是，士衡再劾坤，謂潛進《閨範圖說》，結納宮闈，因請舉冊立、冠婚諸禮。
