translations.literal: Previously, Shiheng had again impeached Kun, charging that he had secretly presented the "Illustrated Expositions on Women's Virtues," cultivated ties within the inner palace, and thereby called for the holding of investiture, capping, and wedding rites.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shiheng had again impeached Lu Kun, alleging that he had secretly submitted the Illustrated Expositions on Women's Virtues, cultivated connections within the inner palace, and thereby pressed for the performance of investiture, capping, and wedding ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 至是有跋《閨範》後者，名曰《憂危竑議》，誣坤與貴妃從父鄭承恩、戶部侍郎張養蒙、山西巡撫魏允貞、吏科給事中程紹、吏部員外郎鄧光祚及道亨、所知等同盟結納，羽翼貴妃子。

translations.literal: At this time there appeared a postscript to the "Women's Virtues" entitled the "Youwei Jiong Memorial," which falsely accused Kun of entering a clique with the Noble Consort's maternal uncle Zheng Chengen, Vice Minister of Revenue Zhang Yangmeng, Grand Coordinator of Shanxi Wei Yunzhen, Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Office Cheng Shao, Vice Director of Personnel Deng Guangzuo, and Daoheng, Suozhi, and others, to support the Noble Consort's son.
translations.idiomatic: At this point a postscript to the Women's Virtues appeared, called the Youwei Jiong Memorial, falsely accusing Kun of forming a clique with the Noble Consort's maternal uncle Zheng Chengen, Vice Minister of Revenue Zhang Yangmeng, Grand Coordinator of Shanxi Wei Yunzhen, Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Office Cheng Shao, Vice Director of Personnel Deng Guangzuo, and Daoheng, Suozhi, and others to bolster the Noble Consort's son.

sentences.zh: 承恩大懼。

translations.literal: Chengen was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen was terrified.

sentences.zh: 以坤、道亨、所知故與士衡有隙，而全椒知縣樊玉衡方上疏言國本，指斥貴妃，遂妄指士衡實為之，玉衡與其謀。

translations.literal: Because of old grudges with Shiheng over Kun, Daoheng, and Suozhi, and because Fan Yuheng, magistrate of Quanjiao, had just submitted a memorial on the succession question denouncing the Noble Consort, they falsely claimed that Shiheng had actually written it and that Yuheng had conspired with him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of old enmity between them and Shiheng over Kun, Daoheng, and Suozhi, and because Fan Yuheng, magistrate of Quanjiao, had just submitted a memorial on the succession denouncing the Noble Consort, they falsely claimed that Shiheng had actually authored it and that Yuheng had plotted with him.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，貴妃復泣訴不已，夜半傳旨逮下詔獄拷訊。

translations.literal: The Emperor was shaken with rage; the Noble Consort again wept and pleaded without cease, and at midnight an edict was transmitted ordering their arrest and interrogation in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was shaken with rage. The Noble Consort wept and pleaded again without end, and at midnight an edict was transmitted ordering their arrest and interrogation in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 比明，命永戍士衡廉州、玉衡雷州。

translations.literal: By dawn, he ordered Shiheng permanently exiled to Lianzhou and Yuheng to Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn he ordered Shiheng permanently exiled to Lianzhou and Yuheng to Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 御史趙之翰復言：「是書非出一人，主謀者張位，奉行者士衡，同謀者右都御史徐作、禮部侍郎劉楚先、國子祭酒劉應秋、故給事中楊廷蘭、禮部主事萬建昆也。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Zhihan again said: "This book did not come from one man alone. The chief plotter was Zhang Wei; the one who carried it out was Shiheng; the co-conspirators were Right Censor-in-Chief Xu Zuo, Vice Minister of Rites Liu Chuxian, Chancellor of the Imperial Academy Liu Yingqiu, the late Supervising Secretary Yang Tinglan, and Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Rites Wan Jiankun.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Zhihan again said, "This book did not come from one man alone. The chief plotter was Zhang Wei; the one who carried it out was Shiheng; the co-conspirators were Right Censor-in-Chief Xu Zuo, Vice Minister of Rites Liu Chuxian, Chancellor of the Imperial Academy Liu Yingqiu, the late Supervising Secretary Yang Tinglan, and Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Rites Wan Jiankun.

sentences.zh: 諸臣皆位心腹爪牙，宜並斥。」

translations.literal: All these officials were Zhang Wei's trusted confidants and henchmen, and should be expelled together."
translations.idiomatic: All these officials were Zhang Wei's trusted confidants and henchmen and should be expelled together."

sentences.zh: 帝入其言，下之部院。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his words and referred the matter to the ministries and boards.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his words and referred the matter to the ministries and boards.

sentences.zh: 時位已落職閑住，署事侍郎裴應章、副都御史郭惟賢力為作等解，不聽。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Wei had already been dismissed and was living in retirement; the acting Vice Minister Pei Yingzhang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Guo Weixian strenuously pleaded on behalf of Zuo and the others, but the Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei had already been dismissed and was living in retirement. Acting Vice Minister Pei Yingzhang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Guo Weixian pleaded strenuously on behalf of Zuo and the others, but the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 奪楚先、作官，出應秋於外，廷蘭、建昆謫邊方，應章等復論救。

translations.literal: Chuxian and Zuo were stripped of office; Yingqiu was posted outside the capital; Tinglan and Jiankun were banished to the frontier; Yingzhang and the others again petitioned for their pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Chuxian and Zuo were stripped of office; Yingqiu was posted outside the capital; Tinglan and Jiankun were banished to the frontier; and Yingzhang and the others again petitioned for their pardon.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，斥位為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased and reduced Zhang Wei to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased and reduced Zhang Wei to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 士衡等再更赦，皆不原。

translations.literal: When amnesties were proclaimed again and again, Shiheng and the others were never pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When amnesties were proclaimed again and again, Shiheng and the others were never pardoned.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，士衡卒於戍所。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, Shiheng died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year, Shiheng died in exile.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史田生金請脫其戍籍，釋玉衡生還，帝不許。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Tian Shengjin requested that Shiheng's exile record be cleared and Yuheng released alive to return home; the Emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Tian Shengjin asked that Shiheng's exile record be cleared and Yuheng released to return home alive; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 曹學程，字希明，全州人。

translations.literal: Cao Xuecheng, styled Ximing, was a native of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xuecheng, styled Ximing, was a native of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知石首、海寧。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Shishou and Haining.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Shishou and Haining.

sentences.zh: 治行最，擢御史。

translations.literal: His administration was rated highest, and he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest in administrative performance, he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 帝命將援朝鮮。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered troops to aid Korea.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered troops sent to aid Korea.

sentences.zh: 已而兵部尚書石星聽沈惟敬言，力請封貢。

translations.literal: Before long the Minister of War Shi Xing, heeding Shen Weijing, strongly urged investiture and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Minister of War Shi Xing, heeding Shen Weijing, strongly urged investiture and tribute.

sentences.zh: 乃以李宗城、楊方亨為正副使，往行冊封禮。

translations.literal: Li Zongcheng and Yang Fangheng were appointed chief and deputy envoys to carry out the investiture ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongcheng and Yang Fangheng were appointed chief and deputy envoys to carry out the investiture ceremony.

sentences.zh: 未至日本，而惟敬言漸不售，宗城先逃歸。

translations.literal: Before they reached Japan, Shen Weijing's words gradually lost credence, and Zongcheng fled home first.
translations.idiomatic: Before they reached Japan, Shen Weijing's assurances gradually lost credence, and Zongcheng fled home first.

sentences.zh: 帝復惑星言，欲遣給事中一人充使，因察視情實。

translations.literal: The Emperor again fell under the sway of Shi's words and wished to send one supervising secretary as envoy to investigate the true situation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again fell under Shi's influence and wished to send a supervising secretary as envoy to investigate the true situation.

sentences.zh: 學程抗疏言：「邇者封事大壞，而方亨之揭，謂封事有緒。

translations.literal: Xuecheng submitted a forceful memorial saying: "Recently the investiture has gone badly awry, yet Fangheng's report claims the investiture is progressing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuecheng submitted a forceful memorial saying, "Recently the investiture has gone badly awry, yet Fangheng's report claims it is making progress.

sentences.zh: 星、方亨表裏應和，不足倚信。

translations.literal: Shi and Fangheng echo each other inside and out; they cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Fangheng echo each other inside and out and cannot be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 為今日計，遣科臣往勘則可，往封則不可。

translations.literal: For the present moment, sending a member of the censorate to investigate is acceptable; sending one to investiture is not.
translations.idiomatic: For the present, sending a censorial official to investigate is acceptable; sending one to investiture is not.

sentences.zh: 石星很很自用，趙誌臯碌碌依違，東事之潰裂，元輔、樞臣俱不得辭其責。」

translations.literal: Shi Xing is stubbornly self-willed; Zhao Zhigao is feckless and indecisive. Neither the chief minister nor the minister of war can evade responsibility for the collapse of affairs in the East."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xing is stubbornly self-willed; Zhao Zhigao is feckless and indecisive. Neither the chief minister nor the minister of war can evade responsibility for the collapse of affairs in the East."

sentences.zh: 初，朝鮮甫陷，御史郭實論經略宋應昌不足任，並陳七不可。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Korea had just fallen, Censor Guo Shi argued that Grand Coordinator Song Yingchang was unfit for the post and set forth seven reasons why he should not serve.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Korea had just fallen, Censor Guo Shi argued that Grand Coordinator Song Yingchang was unfit for the post and set forth seven reasons why he should not serve.

sentences.zh: 帝以實沮撓，謫懷仁典史。

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded Shi as obstructive and demoted him to record keeper of Huairen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor regarded Shi as obstructive and demoted him to record keeper of Huairen.

sentences.zh: 後已遷刑部主事。

translations.literal: Later he had already been transferred to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had already been transferred to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 會封貢議既罷，而朝鮮復懇請之。

translations.literal: When the proposal for investiture and tribute had already been abandoned, Korea again pleaded earnestly for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the proposal for investiture and tribute had already been abandoned, Korea again pleaded earnestly for it.

sentences.zh: 帝乃追怒前主議者，以實倡首，斥為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor then turned his wrath on those who had earlier led the debate, made Shi the chief offender, and reduced him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then turned his wrath on those who had earlier led the debate, made Shi the chief offender, and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 並敕石星盡錄異議者名，將大譴責。

translations.literal: He also ordered Shi Xing to record fully the names of all who had dissented, intending to punish them severely.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Shi Xing to record fully the names of all dissenters, intending to punish them severely.

sentences.zh: 誌臯等力解乃已。

translations.literal: Zhigao and the others pleaded strenuously before he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao and the others pleaded strenuously before he desisted.

sentences.zh: 及遣使不得要領，因欲別遣，已而罷之，即以方亨為正使矣。

translations.literal: When sending envoys yielded no clear result, he wished to dispatch others instead; but this was abandoned, and Fangheng was made chief envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When sending envoys yielded no clear result, he wished to dispatch others instead; but this was abandoned, and Fangheng was made chief envoy.

sentences.zh: 而學程方督畿輔屯田，不知也。

translations.literal: Xuecheng, however, was then supervising military colonies in the capital region and knew nothing of this.
translations.idiomatic: Xuecheng, however, was then supervising military colonies in the capital region and knew nothing of this.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝大怒，謂有暗囑關節，逮下錦衣衛嚴訊。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor was greatly enraged, saying there had been covert interference, and ordered Xuecheng seized and rigorously interrogated by the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor was greatly enraged, alleging covert interference, and ordered Xuecheng seized and rigorously interrogated by the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 榜掠無所得，移刑部定罪。

translations.literal: Torture under the rod yielded nothing; the case was transferred to the Ministry of Justice for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Torture under the rod yielded nothing, and the case was transferred to the Ministry of Justice for judgment.

sentences.zh: 尚書蕭大亨請宥，帝不許，命坐逆臣失節罪斬。

translations.literal: Minister Xiao Daheng requested clemency, but the Emperor refused and ordered execution on the charge of a traitorous subject who had lost his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xiao Daheng requested clemency, but the Emperor refused and ordered execution on the charge of a traitorous subject who had lost his integrity.

sentences.zh: 刑科給事中侯廷佩等訟其冤。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries of the Justice Office Hou Tingpei and others pleaded his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries of the Justice Office Hou Tingpei and others pleaded his innocence.

sentences.zh: 誌臯及陳於陛、沈一貫言尤切，皆不納。

translations.literal: Zhigao, Chen Yubi, and Shen Yiguan spoke most urgently; all were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao, Chen Yubi, and Shen Yiguan spoke most urgently; all were rejected.

sentences.zh: 自是救者不絕，多言其母年九十余，哭子待斃。

translations.literal: From then on pleas for mercy did not cease; many noted that his mother was over ninety and wept for her son awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: From then on pleas for mercy did not cease; many noted that his mother was over ninety and wept for her son awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 帝卒弗聽，數遇赦亦不原。

translations.literal: The Emperor ultimately would not listen; even when amnesties were repeatedly proclaimed, he was not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ultimately would not listen; even when amnesties were repeatedly proclaimed, he was not pardoned.

sentences.zh: 其子正儒，朝夕不離犴狴。

translations.literal: His son Zhengru never left the prison day or night.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengru never left the prison, day or night.

sentences.zh: 見父憔悴骨立，嘔血仆地，久之乃蘇，因刺血書奏乞代父死，終不省。

translations.literal: Seeing his father wasted to bone, he vomited blood and collapsed; long afterward he revived, then wrote a memorial in his own blood begging to die in his father's place, but it was never heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his father wasted to the bone, he vomited blood and collapsed; long afterward he revived, then wrote a memorial in his own blood begging to die in his father's place, but it was never heeded.

sentences.zh: 三十四年九月，始用朱賡言，謫戍湖廣寧遠衛。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirty-fourth year, the Emperor at last heeded Zhu Geng and banished him to serve guard duty at Ningyuan Post in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirty-fourth year, the Emperor at last heeded Zhu Geng and banished him to guard duty at Ningyuan Post in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 久之，放歸，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he was released to return home, and there he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was released to return home, and there he died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，旌正儒為孝子。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign, Zhengru was honored as a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign, Zhengru was honored as a filial son.

sentences.zh: 郭實，字伯華，高邑人。

translations.literal: Guo Shi, styled Bohua, was a native of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shi, styled Bohua, was a native of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授朝邑知縣，選授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Chaoyi, then selected and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Chaoyi, then selected and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 御史王麟趾劾湖廣巡撫秦耀結政府狀，謫徐溝丞。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Linzhi impeached Grand Coordinator of Huguang Qin Yao for currying favor with the central government and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Xu Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Linzhi impeached Grand Coordinator of Huguang Qin Yao for currying favor with the central government and was demoted to assistant magistrate of Xu Gou.

sentences.zh: 實復劾耀，耀乃罷。

translations.literal: Shi again impeached Yao, and Yao was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi again impeached Yao, and Yao was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 比去任，侵贓贖銀巨萬，為衡州同知沈鈇所發，下吏戍邊。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office it was found he had embezzled over ten thousand taels of restitution silver; exposed by Vice Magistrate of Hengzhou Shen Fu, he was handed over to the courts and exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving office it was found he had embezzled over ten thousand taels of restitution silver; exposed by Vice Magistrate of Hengzhou Shen Fu, he was handed over to the courts and exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 故事，撫按贓贖率貯州縣為公費，自耀及都御史李采菲、御史沈汝梁、祝大舟鹹以自潤敗。

translations.literal: By precedent, restitution silver from censorate and surveillance commissioners was generally stored at prefectures and counties for public expenses; from Yao onward, as well as Censor-in-Chief Li Caifei and Censors Shen Ruliang and Zhu Dazhou, all came to ruin through self-enrichment.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, restitution silver from provincial commissioners was generally stored at prefectures and counties for public expenses; from Yao onward, as well as Censor-in-Chief Li Caifei and Censors Shen Ruliang and Zhu Dazhou, all came to ruin through self-enrichment.

sentences.zh: 自是率預滅其籍，無可稽矣。

translations.literal: From then on they habitually expunged the records in advance, so nothing could be audited.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they habitually expunged the records in advance, so nothing could be audited.

sentences.zh: 實以論朝鮮事黜。

translations.literal: Shi was dismissed for his remarks on the Korean affair.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was dismissed for his remarks on the Korean affair.

sentences.zh: 久之，封貢不成，星下吏。

translations.literal: After a long while, when investiture and tribute failed, Shi Xing was handed over to the courts.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, when investiture and tribute failed, Shi Xing was handed over to the courts.

sentences.zh: 給事中侯廷佩請還實官，不許。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Hou Tingpei requested that Shi's office be restored; this was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Hou Tingpei requested that Shi's office be restored; this was refused.

sentences.zh: 家居十五年，起南京刑部主事，終大理右寺丞。

translations.literal: After fifteen years at home he was recalled as Principal Clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and ended as Vice Director of the Right Office of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After fifteen years at home he was recalled as Principal Clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice and ended as Vice Director of the Right Office of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 翁憲祥，字兆隆，常熟人。

translations.literal: Weng Xianxiang, styled Zhaolong, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Xianxiang, styled Zhaolong, was a native of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twentieth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 為鄞縣知縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Yin County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Yin County.

sentences.zh: 課最，入為禮科給事中。

translations.literal: Rated highest in assessment, he entered the Office of Rites as supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest in assessment, he entered the Office of Rites as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 以憂去。

translations.literal: He left office upon bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: He left office upon bereavement.

sentences.zh: 補吏科，疏陳銓政五事。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Office of Personnel, he submitted a memorial setting forth five matters on appointment policy.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Office of Personnel, he submitted a memorial setting forth five matters on appointment policy.

sentences.zh: 其一論掣簽法，言：「使盡付之無心，則天官之職一吏可代。

translations.literal: The first concerned the lottery-drawing method of appointment, saying: "If everything is left entirely to chance, then the duties of the Ministry of Personnel could be performed by a single clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The first concerned the lottery-drawing method of appointment, saying, "If everything is left entirely to chance, then the duties of the Ministry of Personnel could be performed by a single clerk.

sentences.zh: 茍為不然，則地本預擬，何必於大廷中為掩飾之術。

translations.literal: If that is not so, then the posts are predetermined in advance—why resort in the great court to a method of concealment?
translations.idiomatic: If that is not so, then the posts are predetermined in advance—why resort in the great court to a method of concealment?

sentences.zh: 請亟停罷。」

translations.literal: I beg that it be stopped at once."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that it be stopped at once."

sentences.zh: 時不能從。

translations.literal: At the time this could not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this could not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 故事，正郎不奉使，撫按必俟代，至是多反之。

translations.literal: By precedent, full directors did not go on missions, and grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners had to await their replacements; by this time the practice was often reversed.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, full directors did not go on missions, and grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners had to await their replacements; by this time the practice was often reversed.

sentences.zh: 而江西巡撫許弘綱以父憂徑歸，廣西巡撫楊芳亦以憂乞免代，憲祥極言非制。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi Grand Coordinator Xu Honggang returned directly home upon his father's death; the Guangxi Grand Coordinator Yang Fang also asked to be excused from awaiting replacement on grounds of bereavement; Xianxiang forcefully argued this was contrary to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi Xu Honggang returned directly home upon his father's death; Grand Coordinator of Guangxi Yang Fang also asked to be excused from awaiting replacement on grounds of bereavement; Xianxiang forcefully argued this was contrary to regulations.

sentences.zh: 弘綱貶官，芳亦被責。

translations.literal: Honggang was demoted; Fang was also reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: Honggang was demoted; Fang was also reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 言者詆朱賡、李廷機輒被譴，憲祥疏論。

translations.literal: When critics denounced Zhu Geng and Li Tingji and they were repeatedly rebuked, Xianxiang submitted a memorial in their defense.
translations.idiomatic: When critics denounced Zhu Geng and Li Tingji and they were repeatedly rebuked, Xianxiang submitted a memorial in their defense.

sentences.zh: 已，劾雲南巡撫陳用賓、兩廣總督戴耀，並不報。

translations.literal: Later he impeached the Yunnan Grand Coordinator Chen Yongbin and the Grand Coordinator of the Two Guangs Dai Yao; both memorials went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Later he impeached Grand Coordinator of Yunnan Chen Yongbin and Grand Coordinator of the Two Guangs Dai Yao; both memorials went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 是時大僚多缺。

translations.literal: At this time many high offices stood vacant.
translations.idiomatic: At this time many high offices stood vacant.

sentences.zh: 而侍郎楊時喬、楊道賓旬日間相繼物故，吏、禮二部長貳遂無一人。

translations.literal: Within ten days Vice Ministers Yang Shiqiao and Yang Daobin died in succession, and the ministries of Personnel and Rites had not a single chief or deputy left.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Vice Ministers Yang Shiqiao and Yang Daobin died in succession, and the ministries of Personnel and Rites had not a single chief or deputy left.

sentences.zh: 兵部止一尚書，養屙不出。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War had only one minister, who nursed illness and would not appear.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War had only one minister, who nursed his illness and would not appear.

sentences.zh: 戶、刑、工三部暨都察院堂上官，俱以人言註籍。

translations.literal: The ministers and vice ministers of Revenue, Justice, and Works, together with the chief officers of the Censorate, were all suspended from office on public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers and vice ministers of Revenue, Justice, and Works, together with the chief officers of the Censorate, were all suspended from office on public criticism.

sentences.zh: 通政大理亦無見官。

translations.literal: The Office of Transmission and the Court of Judicial Review likewise had no incumbent officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Transmission and the Court of Judicial Review likewise had no incumbent officials.

sentences.zh: 憲祥言九卿俱曠，甚傷國體。

translations.literal: Xianxiang said the Nine Ministers were all vacant, which gravely injured the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxiang said the Nine Ministers were all vacant, which gravely injured the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 因陳補缺官、起遺佚數事，報聞。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted several proposals to fill vacant posts and recall overlooked men of talent; acknowledgment was received.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted several proposals to fill vacant posts and recall overlooked men of talent; acknowledgment was received.

sentences.zh: 屢遷刑科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Justice Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Justice Office.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書孫丕揚、副都御史許弘綱以考察為言路所攻，求去。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Sun Piyang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Honggang, attacked by the remonstrating officials over the personnel evaluation, asked to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Sun Piyang and Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Honggang, attacked by the remonstrating officials over the personnel evaluation, asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 憲祥言：「一時賢者，直道難容，相率引避。

translations.literal: Xianxiang said: "For a time the worthy have found the straight path hard to endure and have withdrawn one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxiang said, "For a time the worthy have found the straight path hard to endure and have withdrawn one after another.

sentences.zh: 國是如此，可為寒心。」

translations.literal: When the state is like this, one cannot but feel chill at heart."
translations.idiomatic: When the state is like this, one cannot but feel chill at heart."

sentences.zh: 既而軍政拾遺，疏為錦衣都督王之楨所撓，久不下。

translations.literal: Later, on matters of military administration he submitted supplementary memorials that were blocked by Embroidered Uniform Guard Commander Wang Zhizhen and long went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on matters of military administration he submitted supplementary memorials that were blocked by Embroidered Uniform Guard Commander Wang Zhizhen and long went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 罪人陳用賓等已論死，疏亦留中。

translations.literal: When the convicted Chen Yongbin and others had already been sentenced to death, his memorial was also retained at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the convicted Chen Yongbin and others had already been sentenced to death, his memorial was also retained at court.

sentences.zh: 憲祥皆抗章論駁。

translations.literal: Xianxiang submitted forceful memorials arguing against all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxiang submitted forceful memorials arguing against all of this.

sentences.zh: 知縣滿朝薦、李嗣善，同知王邦才，以忤稅使系獄，乃請釋之。

translations.literal: Magistrates Man Chaojian and Li Sishan and Vice Magistrate Wang Bangcai, imprisoned for offending the tax commissioner, he asked to have released.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates Man Chaojian and Li Sishan and Vice Magistrate Wang Bangcai, imprisoned for offending the tax commissioner—he asked to have them released.

sentences.zh: 會冬至停決囚，復請推緩刑德意，宥撝臣、矜楚獄。

translations.literal: On the occasion of the winter solstice halt in executions, he again asked that the Emperor extend his virtue of lenient punishment, pardon erring officials, and show mercy to those in prisons far from home.
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion of the winter solstice halt in executions, he again asked that the Emperor extend his virtue of lenient punishment, pardon erring officials, and show mercy to prisoners in distant jails.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不報。

translations.literal: The Emperor responded to none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor responded to none of it.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏科。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，命輔臣葉向高典會試，給事中曾六德以論救被察官坐貶，旨皆從內出。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao to preside over the metropolitan examination; Supervising Secretary Zeng Liude was demoted for pleading on behalf of an official under review—and the rescripts all came from within.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao to preside over the metropolitan examination; supervising secretary Zeng Liude was demoted for pleading on behalf of an official under review—and the rescripts all issued from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 憲祥力諫。

translations.literal: Xianxiang remonstrated forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxiang remonstrated forcefully.

sentences.zh: 中官黃勛、趙祿、李朝用、胡濱等不法，亦連疏彈劾。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Huang Xun, Zhao Lu, Li Chaoyong, Hu Bin, and others acted unlawfully; he also submitted successive memorials impeaching them.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Huang Xun, Zhao Lu, Li Chaoyong, Hu Bin, and others acted unlawfully; he also submitted successive memorials impeaching them.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 居數年卒。

translations.literal: He lived several more years and died.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died.

sentences.zh: 徐大相，字覺斯，江西安義人。

translations.literal: Xu Daxiang, style Juesi, was a native of Anyi in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daxiang, styled Juesi, came from Anyi in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授東昌推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 改武學教授，稍遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to instructor at the military academy and soon promoted to erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to instructor at the military academy and soon rose to erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 四十七年九月朔，百僚將早朝，司禮中官盧受傳免。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month of the forty-seventh year, as the hundred officials were about to attend early court, the Ceremonial eunuch Lu Shou transmitted an order excusing court.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month of the forty-seventh year, as the hundred officials were about to attend early court, the ceremonial eunuch Lu Shou transmitted an order excusing court.

sentences.zh: 眾趨出，受從後姍侮。

translations.literal: The crowd hurried out; Shou followed behind with slow, insulting steps.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd hurried out; Shou followed behind with slow, insulting steps.

sentences.zh: 大相憤，歸草二疏。

translations.literal: Daxiang was indignant; returning home he drafted two memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Daxiang was indignant; returning home he drafted two memorials.

sentences.zh: 一論遼左事，一論受奸邪。

translations.literal: One discussed affairs on the Liaodong frontier; one impeached Shou for wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: One discussed affairs on the Liaodong frontier; one impeached Shou for wicked conduct.

sentences.zh: 時接疏者即受也。

translations.literal: The one then receiving memorials was Shou himself.
translations.idiomatic: The one then receiving memorials was Shou himself.

sentences.zh: 見遼事疏曰：「此小臣，亦敢言事。」

translations.literal: Seeing the Liaodong memorial he said: "This petty official also dares speak on affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Liaodong memorial he said: "This petty official also dares speak on affairs."

sentences.zh: 及帝閱第二疏，顧受曰：「此即論汝罪者。」

translations.literal: When the emperor read the second memorial he turned to Shou and said: "This is the one who impeaches your crimes."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read the second memorial he turned to Shou and said: "This is the one who impeaches your crimes."

sentences.zh: 受錯愕，叩頭流血請罪，曰：「奴當死。」

translations.literal: Shou was startled and abashed; he knocked his head until blood flowed and begged forgiveness, saying: "Your slave deserves death."
translations.idiomatic: Shou was startled and abashed; he knocked his head until blood flowed and begged forgiveness, saying: "Your slave deserves death."

sentences.zh: 疏乃留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was then kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was then kept at court.

sentences.zh: 是日，南京國子學錄喬拱璧亦疏劾受，不報。

translations.literal: That same day Nanjing University Instructor Qiao Gongbi also submitted a memorial impeaching Shou; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Nanjing University instructor Qiao Gongbi also submitted a memorial impeaching Shou; there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷兵部主事。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to principal officer in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to principal officer in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，調吏部稽勛主事，移考功。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was transferred to principal officer of merit records in the Ministry of Personnel, then moved to the bureau of evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tianqi reign he was transferred to principal officer of merit records in the Ministry of Personnel, then moved to the bureau of evaluation.

sentences.zh: 明年，進驗封員外郎。

translations.literal: The next year he advanced to vice director of seal verification.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he advanced to vice director of seal verification.

sentences.zh: 進士薛邦瑞為其祖蕙請謚，大相與尚書張問達議如其請。

translations.literal: Jinshi Xue Bangrui asked a posthumous title for his grandfather Hui; Daxiang and Minister Zhang Wendá deliberated and agreed to the request.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi Xue Bangrui asked a posthumous title for his grandfather Hui; Daxiang and Minister Zhang Wendá deliberated and agreed to the request.

sentences.zh: 熹宗方惡恤典冗濫，鐫大相三秩，出之外。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong was then resentful of redundant and excessive mourning honors; Daxiang was reduced three ranks and sent outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong was then resentful of redundant and excessive mourning honors; Daxiang was reduced three ranks and sent outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 問達等引罪，不問。

translations.literal: Wendá and others cited guilt; they were not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Wendá and others cited guilt; they were not investigated.

sentences.zh: 大學士葉向高、都御史趙南星等連疏救，乃改鐫二秩。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao, Censor-in-Chief Zhao Nanxing, and others submitted successive memorials in his defense; the reduction was changed to two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao, censor-in-chief Zhao Nanxing, and others submitted successive memorials in his defense; the reduction was changed to two ranks.

sentences.zh: 大相方候命，群奄黨受者數十輩，持梃噪於門。

translations.literal: Daxiang was just awaiting his order when several dozen eunuch partisans of Shou, carrying clubs, made a clamor at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Daxiang was just awaiting his order when several dozen eunuch partisans of Shou, carrying clubs, made a clamor at his gate.

sentences.zh: 比搜大相橐，止俸金七十兩，乃哄然散。

translations.literal: When they searched Daxiang's bags they found only seventy taels of salary gold; then they dispersed with a hubbub.
translations.idiomatic: When they searched Daxiang's bags they found only seventy taels of salary silver; then they dispersed with a hubbub.

sentences.zh: 家居，杜門讀書，裏人罕見其面。

translations.literal: Living at home, he shut his door to read; townspeople rarely saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: Living at home, he shut his door to read; townspeople rarely saw his face.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：神宗中年，德荒政圮。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: In the middle years of Emperor Shenzong, virtue was abandoned and government collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist says: In the middle years of Emperor Shenzong, virtue was abandoned and government collapsed.

sentences.zh: 懷忠發憤之士，宜其激昂抗詞以匡君失。

translations.literal: Men who cherished loyalty and gave vent to indignation—it was fitting that they should speak boldly in opposition to correct their ruler's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Men who cherished loyalty and gave vent to indignation—it was fitting that they should speak boldly in opposition to correct their ruler's faults.

sentences.zh: 然納諫有方，務將以誠意。

translations.literal: Yet there is a proper way to accept remonstrance, and one must employ sincere intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there is a proper way to accept remonstrance, and one must employ sincere intent.

sentences.zh: 絞訐摩上，君子弗為。

translations.literal: To wrangle and nitpick while wearing down the sovereign—the gentleman does not do this.
translations.idiomatic: To wrangle and nitpick while wearing down the sovereign—the gentleman does not do this.

sentences.zh: 謂其忠厚之意薄，而衒沽之情勝也。

translations.literal: One may say their thick and honest intent ran thin while the impulse to display and court reputation prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: One may say their thick and honest intent ran thin while the impulse to display and court reputation prevailed.

sentences.zh: 雒於仁、馬經綸詆譏譙讓，幾為儕偶所不能堪矣。

translations.literal: Luo Yuren and Ma Jinglun reviled and reproached with such vehemence that their peers could scarcely bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yuren and Ma Jinglun reviled and reproached with such vehemence that their peers could scarcely bear it.

sentences.zh: 聖人取諷諫，意者殆不如是乎！

translations.literal: When the sage accepts indirect admonition, his intent is probably not like this!
translations.idiomatic: When the sage accepts indirect admonition, his intent is probably not like this!
